relations.name: Kintech
relations.note: The Nerulian-led weapons firm whose equipment fills the fleet's holds, behind a mutual denial no serious analyst believes. The connection is the worst-kept secret in the region.

relations.name: The Alliance
relations.note: The power whose border lanes the fleet raids, and the inheritor of the galaxy the Nerulians lost. The raiding is commerce; the resentment beneath it is personal.

relations.name: Sirius
relations.note: The commercial system whose asteroid belt is widely believed to hide a major pirate staging point, never located, feeding operations across Alliance space.

known_for: Largest organised pirate fleet in the known galaxy
Predominantly Nerulian crews operating from San Tien
Equipment overlap with Kintech products, basis for ongoing intelligence assessment of the connection
The Sirius asteroid base rumour, persistent, widely credited, never confirmed
Operational range that reaches well into Alliance border systems
factions.legal_standing: Illegal throughout all Alliance and affiliated jurisdictions

catalogue_systems.name: Orion System
catalogue_systems.desc: Orion is the political and corporate centre of the known galaxy, and the only capital anyone ever built from scratch. Its worlds run the whole span from a humble trade station to a gleaming artificial capital to a war-scarred survivor to an unfinished frame that will never be completed. It is the seat of the Galactic Union and the tomb of OrionWorks, the organisation that built the artificial worlds and, by one persistent account, started the Tronik War. Nowhere in Alliance space is more defended, more surveilled, or more consequential.
catalogue_systems.subtitle: The Built Heart of the Galaxy, Five Worlds From Trade Hub to Tomb
catalogue_systems.quote: "Every other capital in history was handed to its rulers by a planet. Orion the Galactic Union built for itself, one world at a time, and it shows in everything from the skyline to the politics." (GU orientation address)
catalogue_systems.history:
Orion began as a single space station that grew into the busiest trade hub in known space, the structure now called Orion 1. It is still there, though deliberately scaled down once the artificial worlds were finished, trimmed from a sprawling megastructure into something the GU could actually keep running.
The artificial worlds came next, and they came hard. Orion 2 was the first true attempt to build a planet from nothing, and it failed. It is space debris now, fully decommissioned and salvaged for parts while Orion 3 was under construction, but its failure produced something that mattered more than the world would have. To run a planet, OrionWorks built the Ramirez AI, a planetary-scale intelligence created precisely because Orion 2 had proven that nothing smaller could manage the job.
What they learned, and Ramirez, built Orion 3 and Orion 4, the two artificial worlds still in use today. Orion 3 became the gleaming seat of the Galactic Union. Orion 4 became OrionWorks' own world, the most advanced place that ever existed, until the Tronik War. It survives, inhabited and working, but scarred, whole districts sealed behind the damage, while OrionWorks itself did not survive at all.
Orion 5 was meant to be the last and the greatest, the promised land, and it will stay a frame forever, because OrionWorks is gone and no one else can finish it. The same is true of Ramirez. Most of the great AI was lost when its makers fell, and what survived hides in the sealed districts of Orion 4 in fragments, possibly intact and possibly corrupted, treated as a hazard either way. Enough of it was salvaged to keep Orion 3 running. The rest is somebody's problem waiting to happen.
catalogue_systems.politics:
Orion is the seat of the Galactic Union, the largest megacorporation in the galaxy, and it runs on corporate power before any other kind. The GU governs itself here through its own senate and executive council, a self-contained apparatus that is emphatically not the Alliance, however often outsiders confuse the two. The Union does not govern Alliance space. It simply owns so much of what Alliance space runs on that the distinction rarely costs it anything.
Orion 3 is the most surveilled and most politically dense place in the galaxy, where what you know and whom you know outweigh anything you can actually do. Careers and lives turn on associations, the security forces answer fast and finally, and it is a clean, efficient, lethal place to hold power.
Over all of it hangs the ghost of OrionWorks, the organisation that built the worlds and Ramirez, and that one persistent account blames for starting the Tronik War. The GU does not encourage the question, partly from discretion and partly because the answer lies in the same sealed districts where the broken pieces of Ramirez still stir.

dominant_race.name: The Capital Class, and the Understrata Beneath It
dominant_race.lore:
Orion has no native population, only the most cosmopolitan and most political one in the galaxy. Every power that matters keeps a presence on Orion 3, and around them turns a vast working population of administrators, financiers, fixers, and functionaries, the people who operate the machinery of galactic power and live or die by proximity to it.
Beneath them is the Understrata, the labour and the service and the maintenance that an artificial capital requires without pause, much of it Non-Born and automated. The gleaming city above is real, and so is the fact that it sits on the shoulders of people it is built not to notice. On Orion the senate debates, the Galactic Union decides, and the staff who clean the halls hear both.

race_standing.note: The Galactic Union is, at its core, a human institution, and Orion is the seat of the power humans built. They run it from the top and staff it from the bottom, and a human with the right associations can climb further here than anywhere.

Master politicians in the one arena built for politics. The Patriark are deeply woven into Orion's power games and are among the very few who can play the long game against the GU and not simply lose. Indispensable, and never quite trusted.
Prized through the financial and intelligence machinery of the GU, where reading a room or a market is worth a fortune. Valued, used, and kept to the analytical end of the building.
Menace counts for little in a city run on information and influence, and a Nerulian draws surveillance from the moment they dock. Tolerated, watched, and rarely comfortable.
Security, couriers, and quiet enforcement for players who need things moved or people watched. A capital this political always has work for fast, discreet hands.
The muscle behind the powerful, standing in the doorways of people who can afford the very best. Respected for exactly what they are.
Rare, and valued as bodyguards and brokers whose word holds in a city where almost no one's does. Trust is scarce on Orion, which makes a Skalander worth a great deal.

The capital runs on Non-Born labour and always has. The artificial worlds were built and are maintained by the Non-Born and the machines, and the Understrata that keeps Orion alive is largely theirs. The most powerful place in the galaxy rests on the people it notices least.

relations.name: The Galactic Union
relations.note: The largest megacorporation in the galaxy, headquartered in the capital it built. Orion is the GU made solid, corporate power given an address.

relations.name: The Alliance
relations.note: The political union of Alliance space, a separate institution that outsiders constantly mistake for the GU. Both keep a presence on Orion, the galaxy's political centre, and the GU is careful to remain the power that owns the room rather than the one that governs it.

relations.name: OrionWorks
relations.note: The defunct builders of the artificial worlds and of Ramirez, whose legacy keeps Orion standing and whose possible hand in starting the Tronik War keeps it quiet. The system is as much their tomb as the GU's seat.

relations.name: Arms Corp & Yamato
relations.note: The other two powers of the Big 3, keeping their presence on Orion as they must. The GU is first among the three and takes care never to be heard saying so.

catalogue_systems.gm_notes: Run Orion as the built heart of corporate power, clean and gleaming and watched by everyone. Influence is the currency, surveillance is total, and the dangerous mistake is never a drawn weapon but a wrong association. Keep the GU and the Alliance distinct in play: the Union owns, the Alliance governs, and on Orion it is the owning that decides things. The system's two great mysteries are built for campaigns, whether OrionWorks started the Tronik War, an answer the GU has buried, and what remains of Ramirez, the planetary AI that once ran these worlds, now broken into fragments in the sealed districts of Orion 4, possibly intact, possibly corrupted, and hazardous either way. Salvage into those districts is the classic high-risk run.

planets.name: Orion 1
planets.type: Space Station, Spaceport & Trade Hub (Scaled Down)
planets.atm_note: Maintained throughout commercial sections, outer salvaged ring retains hard vacuum in unrepaired zones
planets.temperature: Climate-controlled interior, around 18°C to 22°C; exterior is hard vacuum
planets.grav_note: Artificial gravity throughout commercial core, patchy in outer salvaged sections
planets.population: ~850,000 permanent staff, transit crews and traders
planets.demographics: Highly mixed, all races, heavy transient population, significant Non-Born labour presence
planets.government: GU Spaceport Authority (civilian) / Alliance Navy Garrison Command (military)
planets.economy: Interstellar trade, cargo transit, warehousing, ship servicing, military logistics
planets.access_note: Open entry with standard Alliance ID check. GU Archive section requires Level 2 clearance. Military substations are restricted.
hazards: Structural mismatch, old salvaged frames next to new construction create unpredictable load stress
Vacuum exposure in outer ring sections not yet repaired
Crowding and crime in the commercial transit zones
Intelligence operations from multiple factions, the volume of trade makes surveillance difficult to avoid

notable_locations.name: Commercial Transit Core
notable_locations.desc: The beating heart of Orion 1's trade operation. Multiple docking arms, warehousing, traders and brokers operating day-cycle around the clock. The busiest single transit point in the Orion system.

notable_locations.name: Military Substations (Network)
notable_locations.desc: The Alliance navy operates a distributed network of substations throughout the station's structure, each positioned to control approach vectors into the system. Well-armed, permanently staffed, and not welcoming to casual visitors.

notable_locations.name: GU Historical Archive
notable_locations.desc: One of the original founding modules, preserved in place amid the commercial sprawl that grew up around it. The Galactic Union charter was signed here. Access Level 2. Some records are restricted with no explanation on file.

notable_locations.name: The Salvaged Ring
notable_locations.desc: The outer sections never rebuilt after materials were stripped for the artificial world projects. Some corridors are hard vacuum. Others have been squatted by traders who prefer not to be registered. The GU Spaceport Authority maintains minimal presence here.

hooks: It is widely known among freight brokers that cargo manifests at Orion 1 routinely list consignees that cannot be verified, a practice so common that customs staff treat it as standard rather than suspicious. Experienced traders say the real consignee is never the registered one.

Scholars studying the original GU charter have long noted that access records for the Historical Archive do not correlate with any documented visitor logs, suggesting routine off-record access by parties whose identities are deliberately excluded from the official register.

Station workers who have served long rotations at Orion 1 say the military substations conduct silent lockdowns periodically with no prior notice and no explanation filed afterward. The practice is so well-established that the civilian staff have developed their own informal warning system to avoid being caught in restricted corridors.
planets.desc: Orion 1 is the station that started everything, the trade hub the whole system grew out of. It is still in use, but deliberately scaled down once the artificial worlds were built, cut back from a sprawling, half-finished megastructure to a leaner spaceport the GU could keep running without waste. It remains one of the busiest transit points in Alliance space, handling the traffic the artificial worlds draw and forwarding most of it onward.

planets.name: Orion 2
planets.atm_note: Core collapsed, no breathable zones remain
planets.temperature: Vacuum; surface swings from roughly -150°C in shadow to +120°C in direct sunlight
planets.grav_note: Fragmented mass, gravitational field unstable and unpredictable
planets.access_note: Active navigational hazard, approach prohibited within 200km
hazards: Gravitational instability, unpredictable micro-gravity wells
High-velocity debris field
No rescue capability within effective range
Electromagnetic interference from core remnants

notable_locations.name: Construction Core Remnant
notable_locations.desc: The original structural skeleton of the failed planet. Partially accessible by skilled pilots but structurally unpredictable. The GU uses it as a cautionary case study in engineering schools.

hooks: Salvagers who have worked the Orion 2 debris field consistently report instrument readings suggesting a power source somewhere in the core remnant, something that should have died with the structure and apparently has not. The GU has never acknowledged these reports.

It is a persistent story among debris field workers that ships sometimes return from the Orion 2 exclusion zone without all the crew that went in. The story is old enough and consistent enough that most veteran salvagers treat it as established fact rather than rumour.

Engineering academics have noted for decades that the GU's official explanation for the Orion 2 failure is inconsistent with the structural data that has been made public. The leading alternative theory among specialists is deliberate sabotage, possibly internal, that the GU has never been willing to investigate openly.
planets.desc: Orion 2 was the Galactic Union's first attempt to build a planet from nothing, and it failed. When Orion 3 went into construction the GU decommissioned Orion 2 entirely and salvaged it for parts, so what remains today is a charted debris field and a navigational caution, nothing more. Its real legacy is not a world but a mind: the failure of Orion 2 was what convinced OrionWorks that running a planet needed an intelligence on a planetary scale, and so it built Ramirez.

planets.name: Orion 3
planets.atm_note: Fully engineered, maintained at precise composition
planets.temperature: Temperate, roughly 0°C to 30°C
planets.grav_note: Artificially generated and maintained, highly stable
planets.demographics: Mixed, all playable races, heavily cosmopolitan
planets.economy: Administration, finance, corporate HQ, legal services, high-end manufacturing
planets.access_note: Visitor permits mandatory, background checks standard. Certain districts require additional clearance.
hazards: Pervasive surveillance, assume all public conversations monitored
Corporate espionage operations constant, multiple competing cells active
Political intrigue, wrong associations can end careers or lives
Security forces react fast and with lethal force

notable_locations.name: GU Senate Chambers
notable_locations.desc: The central legislative body of the Galactic Union. Open sessions attended by representatives from every member system. The real decisions are made elsewhere.

notable_locations.name: Central Treasury
notable_locations.desc: The financial heart of the GU. Manages the largest reserve of credits and physical assets in the galaxy. Effectively impregnable.

notable_locations.name: Corporate Quarter
notable_locations.desc: The district where every major corporation maintains its primary GU offices. Heavily policed, intensely political. The density of power here is difficult to overstate.

notable_locations.name: The Understrata
notable_locations.desc: The lower levels of Orion 3, maintenance corridors and service infrastructure housing the city's underclass. Off the tourist maps but very much part of the economy.

specialties.name: GU Credit & Clearing
specialties.desc: The galaxy's money is issued and cleared through Orion 3. The single most important financial function in known space happens here, quietly, behind doors most visitors never see.

specialties.name: Access
specialties.desc: Orion's true commodity. Not goods but influence, the introductions, clearances, and quiet words that move the galaxy. It is sold constantly and never advertised, and it costs far more than credits.

hooks: The Central Archive on Orion 3 is believed by investigators and financial analysts to hold records of every major corporate transaction in the past two centuries that the GU officially denies retaining. Anomalies in publicly accessible financial histories can only be explained by the existence of such records, and the GU has never provided an alternative explanation.

It is a well-established pattern among Orion 3 traders and couriers that certain GU senators maintain off-manifest freight operations through the station's commercial core. The contents are never discussed and the destinations are never the same twice, but the practice is consistent enough to have its own informal name in the freight community.

Career diplomats and GU intelligence analysts who have served on Orion 3 for long periods speak privately of colleagues who raised questions about Orion 4 and subsequently disappeared from official personnel records, not transferred, not retired, simply absent from any system that can be checked.
planets.desc: Orion 3 is proof that the Galactic Union learns from its failures. Built using everything salvaged from Orion 2, it was the first fully successful artificial planet ever constructed and has stood for centuries. The GU operates its core functions here, executive councils, primary treasury, largest corporate campus, and the administrative infrastructure that ties together the most powerful organisation in the known galaxy. The planet is clean, efficient, and extraordinarily dense with power. Every major corporation has an office here. Security is absolute.

planets.name: Orion 4
planets.atm_note: Maintained in the living districts; the sealed war-scarred sectors are breached and run to vacuum
planets.temperature: Highly variable by region, roughly -30°C to 40°C
planets.grav_note: Gravity generators still functional in some districts, fails without warning in others
planets.population: ~1.5 billion in the functioning districts; the sealed sectors are unpopulated hazard zones
planets.demographics: Mixed, all races; a working population over a buried ruin
planets.government: Galactic Union administration in the living districts; the sealed sectors go unadministered
planets.tech_level: Variable (Cutting-Edge remnants in ruins / Primitive survival conditions in inhabited zones)
planets.economy: Manufacturing, research, GU administration, and the dangerous salvage of OrionWorks technology
planets.access_note: Open to the living districts under GU clearance. The sealed sectors are restricted hazard zones, and the restriction is enforced.
hazards: Sealed war-damaged districts, breached to vacuum and structurally unsound
Surviving fragments of the Ramirez AI in the sealed sectors, possibly corrupted, treated as an active hazard
Unsecured OrionWorks technology, some of it still powered
GU security around the classified districts, fast and unsentimental

notable_locations.name: OrionWorks Research Campus (Ruins)
notable_locations.desc: The former home of the most technologically advanced research organisation in the galaxy. Most is destroyed. Some is not. What remained in the labs when everyone left is an open question.

notable_locations.name: The Pressurised Zones
notable_locations.desc: Six districts that still maintain atmosphere and gravity. Populated by salvagers, squatters, and people with very good reasons not to be anywhere that has a census.

notable_locations.name: Sector 7 (Classified)
notable_locations.desc: A GU-marked restricted zone in the heart of the former research campus. No public documentation exists on what is there. GU patrols actively redirect anyone approaching it.

specialties.name: OrionWorks Salvage
specialties.desc: Technology recovered from Orion 4's sealed districts, the most advanced work the galaxy has ever produced and the most dangerous to handle. Some of it still functions, which is exactly the problem. Priced for the risk and the rarity both.

hooks: Among salvagers who work Orion 4, it is common knowledge that certain sections of the OrionWorks campus were not destroyed in the Tronik War but were deliberately sealed, and that the GU has quietly maintained that sealing ever since while officially claiming the ruins are simply too dangerous to clear.

The GU maintains an unlisted team on Orion 4 that does not appear in any accessible personnel database. This is known among veteran salvagers and squatter communities who have observed their movements and learned to avoid the districts where they operate.

It is reported by multiple independent sources across decades that something in the ruins of OrionWorks continues to broadcast on communication frequencies that only OrionWorks used, frequencies that have been officially retired and should have no active transmitters. The GU has consistently declined to comment on the reports.
planets.desc: Orion 4 was OrionWorks' own world, once the most advanced place that ever existed, and the Tronik War nearly ended it. What remains is a working artificial world with a tomb sealed inside it: living districts, fully inhabited and administered by the GU, wrapped around whole sectors locked away behind the war damage. OrionWorks is gone, but its machines are not entirely gone with it. Fragments of Ramirez, the AI built to run the world, still stir in the sealed districts, and whether they are intact or corrupted is a question no one has been paid enough to answer.

planets.name: Orion 5
planets.atm_note: Frame only, no life support infrastructure installed
planets.temperature: Vacuum; surface swings from roughly -150°C in shadow to +120°C in direct sunlight
planets.grav_note: Structural skeleton only, no gravity systems installed
planets.access_note: Construction zone designation, no authorised civilian access. Frame is completely unsecured.
hazards: No life support, full EVA required throughout
Loose construction materials
Structural instability in incomplete sections
Long-term vacuum exposure in all areas

notable_locations.name: Primary Superstructure Hub
notable_locations.desc: The central node of the planetary frame. The engineering work here represents the height of OrionWorks' design capability. Everything connects to this point. Nothing beyond it has ever been installed.

hooks: Among intelligence professionals and certain high-level corporate operatives, Orion 5 has a well-established reputation as the most deniable meeting location in the Orion system, no life support, no surveillance, and total isolation from any observation network. The practice of using it for sensitive meetings is known enough to be considered an open secret in certain circles.

GU procurement analysts have noted that low-volume material orders consistent with Orion 5 construction preparation have appeared in supply chain records intermittently since the project was suspended, never large enough to attract official scrutiny, but consistent enough to suggest someone is maintaining the option to resume.

In the engineering community descended from OrionWorks practitioners, it is widely believed that complete plans for Orion 5 still exist and that the GU has never destroyed them, choosing instead to keep them inaccessible as both an insurance policy and as leverage over anyone who might independently develop the same capability.
planets.desc: Orion 5 exists as a frame. The superstructure is in place, the skeleton of what would have been the most ambitious planetary construction project the GU had ever attempted, designed by OrionWorks at the height of its capability. Then OrionWorks collapsed. The engineers went home or disappeared. The supply chains dried up. That was fifty years ago. Not a single component has been added since. The GU lists it as a suspended project with no scheduled resumption date.

planets.name: Orion Shepherd Belt
planets.temperature: Vacuum; surface swings from roughly -150°C in shadow to +120°C in direct sunlight
planets.grav_note: Aggregate mass negligible, individual bodies range from boulder to 40km diameter
planets.economy: Trace mineral survey activity, no active extraction licensed
planets.access_note: Navigation through the belt is unrestricted but requires piloting clearance. Standard approach corridors are charted and marked.
hazards: High-velocity debris in irregular orbital paths
GU navigation beacons do not cover the inner belt sections
Salvagers operating without licence are periodically encountered
planets.desc: A dense asteroid field occupying the outer orbital band of the Orion system, well beyond the artificial world cluster. Composed primarily of silicate and metallic bodies, it predates OrionWorks construction activity and was left undisturbed when the artificial worlds were built. The GU designates it a navigational caution zone and maintains approach corridor beacons.

planets.name: Orion-G1
planets.atm_note: Hydrogen-helium envelope, no surface, no breathable zones
planets.temperature: Cryogenic cloud tops, roughly -110°C to -180°C; far hotter in the deep atmosphere under pressure
planets.grav_note: Strong gravitational field, atmospheric drag begins well above visible cloud layer
planets.access_note: Approach unrestricted. No infrastructure.
hazards: Gas giant atmospheric pressure lethal to unshielded vessels below cloud layer
Radiation belts from magnetic field
Strong gravitational gradient
Ring debris field extends several planetary radii from the equatorial plane, approach from the poles recommended
planets.desc: A large banded gas giant in the outer Orion system, designated G1 on GU navigational charts. Distinguished by a prominent ring system of ice and silicate debris, visible from considerable distance and a navigational landmark on approach to the system. The rings are broad but thin, and the amber banding of the planet beneath them makes the combination visually striking. Occasionally used as a gravitational slingshot point by ships on fuel-conserving trajectories. Ring debris fields make equatorial approach inadvisable.

planets.name: Orion-G2
planets.atm_note: Methane-ammonia ice envelope
planets.temperature: Extreme cold, roughly -180°C to -210°C in the upper atmosphere
planets.access_note: Outermost catalogued body. No approach infrastructure.
hazards: Extreme cold, surface equivalent temperatures approach absolute minimum
Methane ice storms in upper atmosphere
Significant distance from any rescue or resupply capability
planets.desc: The outermost body in the Orion system, a dark, methane-blue ice giant sitting at the edge of the star's gravitational influence. GU survey craft have passed it but no permanent observation has been established. Its primary value to navigators is as a distance reference point when plotting inbound approaches.

catalogue_systems.name: Titania System
catalogue_systems.desc: Titania is defined by morondium, a living crystalline compound that grants metals a slow regenerative property when infused, found nowhere else in the galaxy. Every major corporation wants it, so the system is a permanent ground war fought under a strict no-orbital-fire agreement, with Nova-class cruisers hanging overhead as the threat that keeps everyone honest. The Alliance Navy is based here and outgunned here. Only Titania 4 has breathable air, and it is the one neutral ground in a system that exports two things: morondium and the soldiers the war forges.
catalogue_systems.subtitle: The Galaxy's Only Morondium, and the War No One Is Allowed to Win
catalogue_systems.quote: "There are two ways to leave Titania, with a contract or in pieces. The ones who leave with a contract never have to look for work again." (recruiter's pitch, Titania 4)
catalogue_systems.history:
Titania's whole history is morondium. The compound is a living crystal that, infused into metal, lends it a slow regenerative property nothing else can match, and it is found on no other world. Every corporation that matters wanted it, and the wanting turned into a war that escalated past anyone's control until Titania Prime, the largest inhabited world in the system, was destroyed. No one has ever claimed responsibility. The debris field is what the powers point to whenever someone suggests the gloves should come off again.
Out of that catastrophe came the present arrangement. The fighting was confined to the ground, to the morondium seams of Titania 2, under a no-orbital-fire agreement enforced from above by Nova-class cruisers. The Alliance Navy keeps its command in the system, but it does not hold the balance of force: Yamato and the Galactic Union both field Nova-class battlecruisers the navy cannot answer. Whether the absence of orbital bombardment is the navy's doing or simply that no one will destroy the last morondium in the galaxy is argued in every officers' mess in the system and settled in none.
catalogue_systems.politics:
Titania has no single government. Titania 2 is carved among rival corporate armies grinding over the morondium seams; Titania 4 runs on a multi-corporate neutral administration; and the Alliance Navy sits over all of it with the title of authority and not quite the firepower to enforce it.
The real law of the system is the no-orbital-fire agreement. No one strikes from orbit, no one fires on the morondium itself, and no one touches Titania 4. It holds not because the navy compels it but because everyone profits from morondium and no one profits from a second dead world. The Nova cruisers overhead are less a police force than a mutual hostage: each fleet guarantees that if anyone breaks the rule, everyone loses at once.
In its grim way it is stable. The war on Titania 2 never ends, because no one can afford to win it outright and no one will let a rival win it either. The morondium keeps flowing because the fighting stays on the ground. And the Alliance keeps its flag overhead because taking it down would force the megacorps to say out loud who actually runs the system. Everyone has agreed, without once saying so, to keep the war the exact size it already is.

dominant_race.name: The Warriors of Titan
dominant_race.lore:
Titania has almost no civilian population. Its people are soldiers, the logistics crews that arm and feed them, and the medics and traders of Titania 4 who put them back together between rotations. They come from every corporate army and a dozen mercenary outfits, and most are here on a contract that ends one of two ways.
A tour on Titania is a qualification in itself. Anyone who has served here is called a Warrior of Titan, and the name is a mark of hard competence that follows them for the rest of a career. Mercenaries who survive a Titania contract are prized across Alliance space and price themselves accordingly, which is the system's quiet second export. Titania sells the morondium, and it sells the people the morondium war forges, assuming they live long enough to trade on the experience.

race_standing.note: The bulk of every corporate army and most of the mercenary outfits. On Titania a human is a soldier until proven otherwise, and judged by how they handle the ground war.
Nearly impossible to kill in a melee and built to hold a line, which makes a Jaulaus worth a squad on Titania 2. Corporate armies and merc outfits bid for them.
Fast, lethal, and made for the close, brutal work the ground-only war demands. Prized as shock troops and raiders, and expensive once they have a Titania tour behind them.
Honour-bound warriors in a place that runs on the trade of violence. Respected on every side, and valued as the rare merc whose word survives a change of employer.
Their menace and their old reputation make them feared on the line and useful as enforcers. Hired widely and liked nowhere.

Rare on the ground and common in the negotiations, brokering contracts and quietly representing interests that prefer not to be named. The soldiers distrust anyone who profits from the war without bleeding in it.

Cheap, replaceable, and fielded in numbers by corporate armies that count casualties as a line item. A Non-Born soldier on Titania is seldom expected to become a Warrior of Titan, because seldom expected to survive.
Valued for battlefield coordination and logistics, and unsettling in a foxhole. Hired for the command tent more than the front line.

relations.name: The Alliance Navy
relations.note: Holds the title of authority over Titania and not quite the firepower to back it, since Yamato and the Galactic Union both field Nova-class battlecruisers it cannot match. It keeps the peace it can and takes credit for the peace it cannot.

relations.name: Yamato & the Galactic Union
relations.note: The two megacorp powers whose Nova-class cruisers hang over Titania, each strong enough to break the no-orbital-fire agreement and each certain the other would make it pay. Their standoff is the real reason the morondium survives.

relations.name: The corporate armies
relations.note: The rival forces grinding over the morondium seams of Titania 2, fighting a war built never to end and buying soldiers and matériel without pause.

relations.name: Titania 4 neutral administration
relations.note: The one neutral ground in the system, kept inviolate by mutual interest. Everyone repairs and recruits and rests there, because a system this lethal cannot run without a single place that is off-limits.

catalogue_systems.gm_notes: Run Titania as a war that cannot be won and is not allowed to end. The no-orbital-fire agreement is the spine of every scene: overwhelming force sits in orbit and no one dares use it, so the violence happens on the ground, personal and brutal, while the Nova cruisers loom as a threat no one will carry out. Two ways onto the board: the morondium of Titania 2, which everyone wants and no one can hold, and Titania 4, the neutral world where enemies drink at the same counter and a knife in the wrong place could end the truce. And lean on the merc economy, where a Warrior of Titan is both a credential and a target, and the question 'who did you serve with on Titania' opens doors and old wounds in equal measure.

planets.name: Titania Prime
planets.atm_note: Completely destroyed, debris field only
planets.temperature: Vacuum; surface swings from roughly -150°C in shadow to +120°C in direct sunlight
planets.grav_note: Fragmented, residual unstable gravity wells from largest debris masses
planets.access_note: Active navigational hazard, military exclusion zone. Alliance navy enforces standoff.
hazards: High-velocity debris field, extreme navigation hazard
Residual weapons contamination from the corporate war
Unpredictable gravitational micro-wells
Classified: unknown contamination reported in outer debris ring

notable_locations.name: The Graveyard (Inner Ring)
notable_locations.desc: The densest section of the debris field, where the largest planetary fragments cluster. Rich in recoverable materials but extraordinarily dangerous to navigate without specialised equipment.

hooks: Salvagers who work near the Titania Prime debris field consistently report finding objects that are clearly manufactured, not ore, not structural wreckage, in sections of the field that should contain nothing but fragmented planetary matter. The reports are old enough and numerous enough that some veteran salvagers treat constructed objects in the debris as an expected find rather than an anomaly.

Three independent historical analyses conducted across different decades have reached the same conclusion: the destruction of Titania Prime was a deliberate choice by one of the corporate factions, a decision that the other planets be denied rather than contested. No corporation has ever acknowledged this. The Alliance's official position is that the cause remains undetermined.

Navigation crews who make regular runs past the Titania debris field have noted for years that a small shuttle type makes consistent runs into the densest section of the field and emerges on a schedule too precise to be salvage work. Who operates it and what it collects has never been publicly established.
planets.desc: Titania Prime was the largest inhabited world in the system before the morondium wars escalated beyond anyone's ability to control. Nobody claims responsibility for what happened to it. The debris field it left behind is a permanent hazard to navigation and a reminder of what happens when corporate warfare operates without limits. The loss of Titania Prime is directly why the current ground-combat-only agreement was reached, everyone looked at what had been done and understood that without rules, the last morondium world would be next.

planets.name: Titania 2
planets.atm_note: Toxic and unbreathable; sealed armour is mandatory, and the flesh-stripping sandstorms make even that a gamble
planets.temperature: Harsh, broadly -30°C to 55°C, scoured by abrasive sandstorms
planets.demographics: Predominantly human, mixed corporate deployments from across known space
planets.government: None, contested control, multi-corporate military administration
planets.economy: Morondium extraction (ongoing despite conflict), military logistics, weapons supply
planets.access_note: Civilian access prohibited. Entry without corporate military credential risks immediate engagement by all parties.
hazards: Flesh-stripping sandstorms that abrade armour and cut visibility to nothing
Active combat operations, all zones contested
Morondium dust inhalation, cumulative neurological toxin
Unexploded ordnance throughout all sectors
Corporate intelligence ops, assume surveillance by multiple parties
Supply interdiction, food and medical resupply are active combat targets

notable_locations.name: The Extraction Zone (Sector 7)
notable_locations.desc: The primary morondium deposit site. Whoever controls this sector controls the only active export point. It changes hands on average twice per week.

notable_locations.name: Forward Operating Bases (Multiple)
notable_locations.desc: Each major corporate faction maintains at least one FOB on Titania 2. Locations shift as territory does. Maps are obsolete within days of issue.

notable_locations.name: The Meatgrinder (Trench Network)
notable_locations.desc: A network of trenches and fortifications in the central plain, established decades ago and never fully abandoned. Some of the oldest sections have become almost permanent infrastructure. Veterans call this place home.

specialties.name: Morondium (Raw)
specialties.desc: The living crystalline compound the whole war is about, cut from the seams of Titania 2 under fire. Infused into metal it lends a slow regenerative property found in no other material, and it exists nowhere else in the galaxy.

hooks: Cross-faction intelligence leaks are so commonplace on Titania 2 that military analysts consider the information environment effectively transparent, every corporate faction assumes its operational plans are known to at least one rival, and plans accordingly. The result is a war fought less on information advantage than on sheer attrition and willingness to take losses.

The most dangerous regular work available in known space is moving material from forward operating bases to extraction ships on Titania 2, a route that crosses multiple contested sectors and changes weekly as territory shifts. The pay reflects this. So does the casualty rate among contractors who take the work.

It is accepted among morondium researchers as near-certain that secondary deposits exist outside the current warzone boundary, geological surveys support this, but the discovery has never been publicly confirmed because anyone who locates one faces an immediate and non-survivable level of corporate interest.
planets.desc: Titania 2 is the most fought-over piece of ground in the known galaxy. Morondium, a living crystalline compound that grants metals regenerative properties when infused, exists nowhere else. The current state of affairs is a permanent ground war between corporate armies operating under a single enforced rule: no orbital strikes, no bombardment, no weapons of mass destruction. Ground forces only. This rule is enforced by a Yamato-class and a GU Nova cruiser in permanent orbit, each with orders to destroy any fleet that attempts an orbital strike. For players, Titania 2 is hell with a purpose. There is always work here for soldiers, medics, engineers, and people who can get things across active fire zones. The world itself fights everyone on it, with a toxic sky and sandstorms abrasive enough to strip flesh and pit armour, so the morondium is bled out of the ground at a cost counted in more than casualties.

planets.name: Titania 4
planets.atm_note: Clean, distance from the warzone keeps atmospheric contamination minimal
planets.temperature: Breathable and mild, roughly 12°C to 28°C, the only comfortable air in the system
planets.population: ~2 million, rotating military and support personnel
planets.demographics: Highly mixed, all corporate factions represented simultaneously
planets.economy: Medical services, rest and recreation, food production, neutral logistics hub
planets.access_note: Universal truce enforced by mutual agreement and profit motive. Violence is handled quietly and away from public areas.
hazards: Intelligence operations from all sides, assume you are being watched at all times
Corporate-sponsored violence occurs but is kept away from areas that would draw attention
Debt collection, Titania 4 is where financial disputes from the warzone get settled
Information is a commodity and a weapon here

notable_locations.name: The Strip
notable_locations.desc: The main commercial district. Bars, clinics, black market vendors, and recreational facilities catering to every taste and budget. The truce holds here because it is too profitable to break.

notable_locations.name: Neutral Medical (NMed)
notable_locations.desc: The largest independent field hospital in the known galaxy. Treats all patients regardless of corporate affiliation. Technically neutral, in practice, the intelligence value of a fully-staffed trauma facility cannot be overstated.

notable_locations.name: The Counting Houses
notable_locations.desc: Financial services district, where corporate contracts are negotiated, morondium futures traded, and the real decisions about Titania 2 are made, off the battlefield.

specialties.name: Warriors of Titan
specialties.desc: The system's other great export: soldiers and mercenaries who have survived a Titania contract. A tour here is a credential that opens any door in the trade, and the ones who live to collect it never want for work.

specialties.name: Neutral-Ground Spirits
specialties.desc: The drink of Titania 4, poured in bars where enemies share a counter under the truce. Rough and strong, and famous less for its quality than for the company it keeps.

hooks: Debt collection on Titania 4 operates in a legal grey area that both corporate factions tolerate because it occasionally works in their favour, soldiers from any side can find themselves held by the other side's financial representatives without it technically constituting a truce violation. This is common enough that experienced fighters carry debt documentation as a matter of personal survival practice.

It has been reported across decades by medical staff who have worked at NMed that the facility is extensively monitored by every major corporate intelligence operation in the system, the patient population makes it the most information-rich location in the Titania theatre. This is treated as an occupational hazard of working there rather than an exceptional situation.

The Counting Houses on Titania 4 are where the real war is conducted, every major territorial shift on Titania 2 below has been preceded by a corresponding shift in the financial instruments traded on Titania 4 above, typically several weeks in advance. Analysts who track both markets simultaneously have predicted engagements before they occurred.
planets.desc: Titania 4 is the eye of the storm. Every corporation with a presence in the system maintains facilities here, and a universal truce holds, enforced not by law but by mutual self-interest and the understanding that if the truce breaks here, the Nova cruisers above Titania 2 become far less predictable. Soldiers from every side come here for medical treatment, rest, food that is not field rations, and a few days of not being actively targeted. The Alliance Navy keeps its system command here too, a guest on neutral ground like everyone else, which tells you most of what you need to know about how much of Titania it truly controls.

planets.name: Carnath
planets.temperature: Vacuum; surface swings from roughly -150°C in shadow to +120°C in direct sunlight
planets.access_note: Unrestricted access. Several corporate survey teams have landed. None have established permanent presence.
hazards: No atmosphere, full EVA required at all times
Micrometeorite impacts more frequent than average due to proximity to Titania Prime debris field
Corporate survey teams operating here may be armed
planets.desc: A small, airless rocky world sitting between the warzone of Titania 2 and the neutral ground of Titania 4. The name Carnath was assigned by a survey team over a decade ago and has stuck in usage despite no official designation process. Its proximity to the Titania Prime debris field means its surface shows heavier cratering than expected for its size. Several corporations have quietly surveyed it for morondium traces but found nothing commercially significant. Occasionally used as an observation post during periods of intense fighting on Titania 2.

planets.name: Veroth
planets.atm_note: Hydrogen-helium gas envelope
planets.temperature: Cryogenic cloud tops, roughly -110°C to -180°C; far hotter in the deep atmosphere under pressure
planets.access_note: No infrastructure. Some vessels use its moons as observation stations.
hazards: Gas giant atmosphere, lethal pressure below cloud deck
Radiation belt
Strong gravitational gradient
Sparse ring system creates navigational scatter zone around equatorial approach
planets.desc: A large banded gas giant in the outer Titania system, informally named Veroth by navigators running the approach corridor. A faint but visible ring system circles the equatorial plane, composed of dark material, less visually striking than Orion-G1 but noted on all current navigational charts. Several of its moons have been proposed as observation or staging platforms for corporate military planning. None have been formally developed, though survey teams have mapped them. Veroth itself is useful primarily as a gravitational reference on approach.

planets.name: Sorellis
planets.temperature: Frozen, roughly -80°C to -30°C
planets.access_note: Extreme outer system. No navigation infrastructure.
hazards: Extreme cold, cryogenic surface temperatures
No atmosphere
Extreme distance from system centre
planets.desc: The outermost known body in the Titania system, named Sorellis in navigational records, a frozen, airless world of water-ice and silicate rock at the very edge of the star's gravitational influence. So remote that even corporate survey teams with resource extraction interests have decided the transit time does not justify the potential return. It sits in permanent darkness, unchanged by everything that has happened in the system closer to the sun.

catalogue_systems.name: Sirius System
catalogue_systems.desc: Sirius is the commercial heartbeat of Alliance Space, a wealthy, densely populated system with some of the busiest spaceports in the galaxy. If you need to buy something, fence something, or find someone, Sirius is the first place to look. Its orbital stations are cities in their own right, and its surface worlds host the headquarters of several major corporations.
catalogue_systems.subtitle: The Galaxy's Marketplace, Neon Laid Over Deep Water
catalogue_systems.quote: "On Sirius you can buy anything: a ship, a senator, a new face, an old enemy's location. The only thing nobody sells is the name of who they answer to." (a Sirius dock-broker, to a first-time visitor)
catalogue_systems.history:
Sirius was always going to be rich. It sits where the trade lanes cross, a temperate ocean world easy to settle and impossible to ignore, and it grew into the commercial heart of Alliance space. Its single ocean-spanning city and its ring of station-cities handle a staggering share of everything bought and sold in known space.
Wealth on that scale draws two kinds of predator, and on Sirius they arrived together and stayed. Yamato, the oldest and most opaque of the Big 3, made the system its home and its mask. The crime families grew up alongside the legitimate trade until telling them apart became a matter of paperwork. Today Sirius runs on an unspoken understanding among the Alliance that governs it on paper, the corporation that owns more of it than anyone can prove, and the families that keep its streets and its seas in profitable order.
catalogue_systems.politics:
On paper Sirius is Alliance territory, governed by the Planetary Council on the surface and the Station Council Federation in orbit, both of them swimming in corporate money. On paper.
In practice power is a three-way balance among the Alliance administration, Yamato's invisible hand, and the crime families, and it holds because all three want the same thing: the trade must keep flowing. Order on Sirius is kept by interest, not by law. The families suppress the kind of chaos that scares off business, Yamato keeps the machinery turning from behind its shell companies, and the Alliance supplies the respectable face that lets everyone pretend the market is clean.
The families run on a code older than the Alliance: rank, loyalty, debt, and face. The Seto Syndicate is the corporate one, a galactic criminal enterprise more disciplined than most real corporations. The Tanaka Syndicate is the street one, brutal and local, and quietly funded by Yamato. Between them they keep a peace the Alliance navy never could, for reasons the navy would rather not examine.
For all that managed order, Sirius suffers the worst piracy in Alliance space, and not by accident. The richest trade lanes make the richest targets, and several pirate clans are based here, working behind legitimate charters as shipping lines and salvage outfits. They prey on the same lanes their paperwork says they serve and launder the proceeds through their own front companies, and the three powers tolerate them so long as they bleed the trade rather than break it. Clearing them out would cost more than they steal, and more than one respectable Sirian fortune began with a hold full of someone else's cargo.

dominant_race.name: Sirians
dominant_race.lore:
Sirius has no native people, only arrivals. Its culture is the most cosmopolitan in Alliance space, and it opens to anyone the moment they have something to trade. Humans are the plurality and the Non-Born a vast presence, but a Sirian cares far less about your species than about your credit and, above that, whose patronage you carry.
Sirians are quick and transactional, charming in the manner of people raised in a market that never closes. They prize the deal and the favour, and the face you show the world, and they take it as given that everyone answers to someone. The city sprawls across archipelagos and floating platform-districts above deep ocean, neon over dark water, and the seas hide as much commerce as the undercity does. It is a glorious place to get rich and an easy place to disappear, often in the same week.

race_standing.note: The plurality and the default face of Sirian commerce. A human with credit and a patron belongs; a human with neither is one more body in an eight-billion-soul city.
A vast community running the logistics and the labour the city floats on. Less openly scorned than on prouder worlds, and still rarely the name on the deal.
Naturals at a game built on patience and leverage, and thick on the ground in station administration. Indispensable, ubiquitous, and trusted about as far as anyone on Sirius trusts anyone.
A people who keep their word are worth their weight in a city of liars. Skalander find steady, well-paid work as brokers and arbiters whose handshake means something.
Couriers, enforcers, and security for shipping lines and syndicates alike. Fast and lethal, and always in demand where someone needs something moved or someone watched.
Dock muscle and bodyguards, the immovable objects behind every door that matters. Respected for exactly what they are.
Their menace makes them prized syndicate enforcers and feared everywhere else. On Sirius that is a marketable skill and a shadow over every room they enter.
They read a market, a contract, or a mark with equal ease, which makes them invaluable in finance and unnerving across a table. Hired often, relaxed around never.

relations.name: Yamato Corporation
relations.note: The invisible hand. Headquartered here and threaded through the system behind its shell companies, Yamato owns more of Sirius than anyone can prove, which is exactly how it prefers things.

relations.name: Seto Syndicate
relations.note: The largest crime family in Alliance space, run like a corporation and keeping order because disorder is bad for business. On Sirius it is less an underworld than a parallel government.

relations.name: Tanaka Syndicate
relations.note: The street-level family, brutal and local, and quietly funded by Yamato. It handles the work Seto considers beneath it, and the muscle the respectable powers prefer not to discuss.

relations.name: The Alliance
relations.note: Governs Sirius on paper and supplies the clean face that lets the market pretend it is clean. Its writ runs exactly as far as the families and Yamato find convenient.

relations.name: Sirius Pirate Clans
relations.note: Several pirate clans are based on Sirius behind legitimate shipping and salvage charters, preying on the very lanes that make the system rich. The three powers tolerate them so long as they bleed the trade rather than break it.

catalogue_systems.gm_notes: Run Sirius as neon over deep water, a glorious and dangerous marketplace where anything is for sale and the law is one bidder among several. Players can buy or fence or find almost anything here, and they can set the three powers against one another, carefully, because all three keep the peace only while chaos stays unprofitable. Lean on the yakuza code: face and debt outrank credits, and an insult can cost more than a theft. The oceans hide as much as the undercity, and on Sirius everyone, including the players' best new friend, answers to someone they have not mentioned.

planets.name: Sirius Prime
planets.atm_note: Heavily managed air quality in upper tiers, pollution a persistent issue in lower districts
planets.temperature: Mild maritime, roughly 12°C to 28°C, warmer in the dense city cores
planets.demographics: Highly mixed, all playable races, significant Non-Born community
planets.economy: Interstellar trade, financial services, corporate HQ, black market, entertainment, manufacturing
planets.access_note: Open entry with standard Alliance identity verification. Criminal records flagged on entry, but flags can be managed.
hazards: Organised crime networks throughout lower districts
Corporate espionage, competing intelligence cells active citywide
Trafficking operations in port districts
Police corruption endemic in certain precincts

notable_locations.name: The Grand Spaceports
notable_locations.desc: Three orbital and two surface terminals processing billions of tons of cargo annually. The busiest single transit points in Alliance Space. Every major trading house maintains a presence here.

notable_locations.name: The Exchange
notable_locations.desc: The galaxy's largest commodities market. What gets priced here affects prices everywhere else. A dozen intelligence agencies maintain listening operations in the building at all times.

notable_locations.name: The Warren (Lower Districts)
notable_locations.desc: The underside of Sirius Prime, old city sections not visible from orbit. Crime organisations, independent operators, and people who need to not be found call the Warren home. Also home to some of the best food in the system.

notable_locations.name: Corporate Row
notable_locations.desc: The headquarters district for several of the galaxy's largest corporations. Publicly accessible, intensely surveilled, and the scene of the most aggressive corporate competition in the galaxy.

specialties.name: Sea-Market Cuisine
specialties.desc: Real ocean-caught seafood from the city's own waters, folded into the most cosmopolitan food scene in known space. Every cuisine of the galaxy meets here, and the best of it is found in stalls that appear on no registry.

specialties.name: Sirian Suntide
specialties.desc: The signature harbour liquor, distilled dockside and served from the platform bars to the orbital lounges. Bright, potent, and poured at every deal worth closing.

specialties.name: Anything, Discreetly
specialties.desc: Sirius's true specialty is access. Genuine, grey, or outright stolen, if a thing exists somewhere in the galaxy a Sirian broker can put it in your hands, no questions asked and every question priced in.

hooks: It is widely understood among freight professionals in the Sirius system that a significant percentage of cargo arriving under Dark Space manifests is misrepresented, the Warren district has absorbed this trade for long enough that receiving handlers consider a false manifest from that origin more reliable than an accurate one from anywhere else.

Financial analysts who specialize in commodity markets have documented for decades that morondium futures on the Exchange show patterns consistent with advance knowledge of military outcomes on Titania 2. The pattern is consistent enough that several academic papers have been published on it, all of which the Exchange has formally disputed without successfully refuting.

The practice of corporate executives arranging quiet extraction from their own organisations' facilities on Sirius Prime is well-established enough that several independent security firms maintain dedicated capability for it. The usual reasons are never shared publicly, but experienced operators say the pattern is almost always the same: someone has found out something about the organisation they work for.
planets.desc: Sirius Prime is the commercial heart of Alliance Space, an ecumenopolis where old city districts layer upon each other across centuries of construction. The upper tiers gleam with corporate towers and efficient transit. The lower levels are a different world entirely. The spaceports never sleep. The Exchange sets the price of half the galaxy's goods. And somewhere in the Warren, every deal that cannot be made in daylight finds its way to a table. For all its towers, Sirius Prime is an ocean world: the ecumenopolis sprawls across archipelagos, reclaimed coasts, and vast floating platform-districts, and the seas between them carry as much cargo, and hide as much of it, as the spaceports above.

planets.name: Sirius Orbital Network
planets.atm_note: Maintained station atmosphere across all connected habitats
planets.temperature: Climate-controlled interior, around 18°C to 22°C; exterior is hard vacuum
planets.grav_note: Artificial gravity throughout, rotational backup in older sections
planets.population: ~500 million, permanent residents across all stations
planets.demographics: Mixed, heavy Non-Born and Patriark presence in administrative roles
planets.economy: Shipping logistics, warehousing, passenger transit, ship servicing, corporate office space
planets.access_note: Most stations open with standard ID check. Corporate-owned sections require corporate affiliation.
hazards: Decompression risk in older station sections
Smuggling operations throughout the cargo logistics chain
Corporate security forces with minimal external oversight
Station politics can turn lethal, committee seats are contested violently

notable_locations.name: Central Hub Station
notable_locations.desc: The largest single structure in the Sirius system. Population rivalling small cities. Contains system-wide control, coordination, and the central customs authority.

notable_locations.name: The Free Docks
notable_locations.desc: Unaffiliated docking sections where small operators, independent traders, and people who prefer not to have their cargo logged operate. Alliance administration maintains minimal presence here by convention.

hooks: Station workers across the Sirius orbital network consistently report that cargo flagged by customs inspectors is regularly cleared through administrative override, a pattern so established that it has its own informal name in dock culture. The cold addresses used as cover destinations recur across years of records, suggesting an ongoing and organised operation rather than isolated incidents.

Shell corporation acquisition of station sections in the Sirius orbital network has been documented repeatedly over the decades, always following the same pattern: quiet purchase, displacement of independent operators, and transition to use by parties who are not publicly identifiable. The independent trader communities who have been displaced rarely remain accessible for follow-up questions.

Insurers who underwrite cargo through the Sirius lanes have known for decades that a large share of the losses they pay out trace back to the same handful of locally chartered shipping and salvage firms, and that those firms are never the ones the Station Council Federation chooses to investigate. The pattern is openly discussed in the trade and quietly absent from every official report.
planets.desc: The Sirius orbital station network is, in practical terms, a series of cities in space. Collectively they house half a billion people, process a significant portion of all interstellar cargo moving through the core systems, and host the offices of dozens of corporations and hundreds of independent operators. The Free Docks at the system's edge are where independent operators work without the scrutiny the main terminals carry.

planets.name: Pyreth
planets.temperature: Extreme heat, roughly +80°C to +300°C
planets.grav_note: Unusually dense core for its size, standard surface gravity despite small diameter
planets.demographics: Mostly Non-Born operators, small human technical rotation
planets.economy: Heavy metal extraction, iron, nickel, platinum-group ore processing
planets.access_note: Corporate property. Contractor access by arrangement. The Consortium discourages unscheduled visits.
hazards: Extreme surface temperatures on daylight side, well above equipment operating limits
No atmosphere, full EVA
Automated mining equipment creates surface hazard zones
planets.desc: A small but exceptionally dense rocky world close to Sirius, known as Pyreth to navigators and mining crews, though the Sirius Mining Consortium's official documentation uses the older navigational designation. Pyreth's unusually dense metallic core makes it valuable despite its size. A skeleton crew of mostly Non-Born operators manages the automated extraction network from a pressurised station on the terminator line. The ore is processed on-world and shipped in bulk to Alliance Space manufacturing systems.

planets.name: Calodan
planets.atm_note: Hydrogen-helium envelope
planets.temperature: Cryogenic cloud tops, roughly -110°C to -180°C; far hotter in the deep atmosphere under pressure
planets.economy: Hydrogen fuel extraction, sells to passing vessels at commercial rates
planets.access_note: Fuel skimming platform open to commercial vessels. Guild-licensed rates apply. Emergency fuel available without prior arrangement.
hazards: Gas giant atmospheric hazards below platform altitude
Radiation belt activity varies
Platform is functional but not designed for extended habitation
planets.desc: Known as Calodan to the navigators and freight crews who fuel here, a large gas giant serving as the primary commercial fuel stop for vessels transiting the Sirius system. A Guild-licensed skimming platform operates in its upper atmosphere, extracting and processing hydrogen at commercial rates. Calodan is one of the busiest non-orbital commercial stops in the system; ships that prefer not to dock at the orbital network, for whatever reason, fuel here instead. The platform crew maintains carefully neutral relationships with everyone.

planets.name: Celendris
planets.atm_note: Methane-water ice envelope
planets.temperature: Extreme cold, roughly -90°C to -40°C
planets.economy: None, theoretical ice mining interest, no active operations
planets.access_note: Outer system, no infrastructure. Alliance survey completed.
hazards: Extreme cold
No infrastructure
Far from system emergency response
planets.desc: An ice giant in the outer Sirius system, named Celendris in navigational records, blue-green in colouration due to methane ice in its upper atmosphere. Alliance survey teams have catalogued it as a candidate for future water-ice extraction but no commercial operation has been established. It sits at the outer edge of the system's charted routes, a pale reference point for ships approaching from the deep system.

catalogue_systems.name: Aderan System
catalogue_systems.desc: The Aderan system was the site of the first corporate war in galactic history, a conflict that ended with Aderan Prime destroyed and everyone finally understanding that there was no upper limit to what corporate warfare could do. The surviving world found a highly profitable replacement economy.
catalogue_systems.subtitle: The First World the Corporations Killed, and the Profitable Afterlife of the One That Lived
catalogue_systems.quote: "Aderan Prime taught the galaxy that corporate war has no ceiling. Aderan 3 taught it something worse: that the survivors could make the ruins pay." (Alliance historian, lecture transcript)
catalogue_systems.history:
Aderan was where corporate rivalry first escalated past conventional warfare into something with no upper limit. The first corporate war in galactic history ended with Aderan Prime, a populated world, destroyed outright. Who fired first is disputed to this day; every corporation involved blames another, and the wreckage has never been recovered or memorialised. The interests that did it simply moved on to the next calculation. The debris field is the quietest warning in the galaxy, and everyone has agreed to stop reading it.
One inhabited world, Aderan 3, survived, and turned catastrophe into a business model. Voran Industries, a failed aerospace firm reborn, took the prison contract and then made the prisoners pay several times over. They became a captive labour force rented to industry, the cast of the galaxy's most-watched broadcasts, and the engine of a consumer brand. Its racing programme, Ridge Racing, is now the single most-watched sport in known space, and the gear that carries its name sells on every world that can receive the signal. Aderan ships punishment to the galaxy as labour, as spectacle, and as merchandise.
catalogue_systems.politics:
Aderan is a corporate possession wearing a justice-system veneer. The Aderan Correctional Consortium, Voran Industries' operating arm, runs Aderan 3 as warden and government and studio together. The planet has no citizens, only the people who work it, the people held in it, and the people watching from somewhere safer.
The business model is the horror. Voran profits from custody and from labour and from spectacle at once, so it profits from more prisoners, longer sentences, and higher ratings, and it has quietly optimised for all of them. Every inmate is also a worker, since Aderan rents its captive workforce to corporations across Alliance space at rates no free labourer could survive, which makes a sentence here a labour contract the prisoner never gets to negotiate. An inmate who draws an audience is managed for screen time instead, because a popular prisoner is worth more on camera than on a work line.
The Alliance ships its problem to Aderan and looks away. Outsourcing justice to a corporation that monetises the cage, the labour, and the carnage suits everyone except the incarcerated, and the incarcerated do not vote. The shows are too popular and the contracts too profitable for anyone with the power to end it to want to.

dominant_race.name: Inmates, Keepers, and Cameras
dominant_race.lore:
Aderan 3 has no native population, only the classes the business runs on: the inmates, who are its inventory and its workforce and its talent; the keepers who manage them; and the cameras that turn the whole thing into revenue. Prisoners arrive from every world, sorted less by their crimes than by their screen potential. The staff are company through and through, paid well enough not to ask questions. Over all of it sits the production apparatus, because on Aderan the difference between a sentence and a season is mostly a matter of editing.
Life here is decided by which side of the camera you are on. For the audience across the galaxy, Aderan is the best entertainment money can buy. For the talent, it is a sentence that ends only when the ratings do.

race_standing.note: The bulk of both the inmate population and the audience. A human on Aderan is a customer, a guard, or content, depending on the paperwork.
Durable, powerful, and almost impossible to put down, which makes a convicted Jaulaus a Blood Bowl producer's dream. Prized as talent for the very trait that ought to earn mercy.
Fast and lethal, cast as the crowd-favourite predators of the arena and the Survivor zones. The Consortium values a Hakari inmate at a premium, and not out of kindness.
Their menace makes them villains the audience loves to hate, and the Consortium casts them on sight. A Nerulian on Aderan is rarely allowed to be anything but the heel.
Cheap, plentiful, and legally murky, which makes Non-Born inmates the most disposable inventory on the books and the least likely to have anyone asking after them.
Rare as inmates and common as silent partners. The Patriark do not end up on Aderan. They own pieces of it, quietly, the way they own pieces of everything.
Honour-bound warriors who now and then arrive as inmates and flatly refuse to perform, which the Consortium finds by turns infuriating and excellent television.
Valued in the production booth for reading audiences and predicting which inmates will draw a crowd. Disturbingly good at it.

relations.name: Voran Industries
relations.note: Aderan is Voran's company system, run through the Aderan Correctional Consortium, warden and government and studio in a single corporate hand.

relations.name: The Alliance
relations.note: Ships its convicts to Aderan, banks the savings, and declines to examine the conditions or the broadcasts. Complicity dressed up as outsourcing.

relations.name: The galaxy's audience
relations.note: Three of the most-watched programmes in known space are filmed here, with Ridge Racing first among them. The viewers are the reason the cages stay full.

catalogue_systems.gm_notes: Run Aderan in two registers. The dead world, Aderan Prime, is a debris-field ghost story, full of salvage and radiation and the buried question of who really fired first, which several powerful parties would rather stayed buried. The live world, Aderan 3, is prison-planet noir with a camera always running, where the most dangerous thing a character can do is become interesting to the producers. Strong plots: a wrongful or purchased inmate, a broadcast escape, exposing the first-corporate-war cover-up, or simply surviving a season. And never forget the incentive that drives the place: the system wants the players inside it, and on screen.

planets.name: Aderan Prime
planets.temperature: No surface; cratered debris in vacuum, roughly -150°C in shadow to +120°C in direct sun
planets.grav_note: Fragmented mass, residual unstable gravity wells
planets.access_note: Navigational hazard designation. No official memorial. Alliance discourages unscheduled approaches.
hazards: Active debris field, navigational hazard rated extreme
Residual weapons contamination in dense sections
Gravitational instability from fragmented core

notable_locations.name: Ground Zero (Estimated)
notable_locations.desc: The approximate centre of the event that destroyed the planet. Several independent groups have placed physical markers here. Alliance navy periodically removes them.

hooks: Among historians who study the first corporate war, it is the consensus view, though unpublished as such, that the Alliance's official position attributing the destruction of Aderan Prime to mutual escalation is a deliberate misrepresentation protecting one specific corporate faction whose successor organisation remains politically active today. The evidence exists in archival records that have changed hands multiple times and are never accessible simultaneously.

It is a recurring feature of the Aderan Prime debris field that corporate legal departments periodically file recovery claims for unspecified assets without ever disclosing what they are seeking. Salvagers who have worked the field say these claims arrive in clusters, suggesting that multiple corporations believe the same thing is in the debris and are each hoping to reach it first.
planets.desc: Aderan Prime was the first world ever destroyed in a corporate war. The event, disputed to this day, with multiple corporations claiming the others fired first, marked a turning point in galactic history: the moment everyone understood that corporate conflict had escalated beyond conventional warfare into something with no natural upper limit. No recovery or memorial operation has ever been mounted. The corporate interests that destroyed it moved on to the next calculation.

planets.name: Aderan 3
planets.atm_note: Standard breathable, Consortium manages atmospheric integrity for broadcast quality
planets.temperature: Engineered by zone: controlled habitats alongside deliberately hostile show "zones", broadly -20°C to 45°C by sector
planets.demographics: Mixed, global inmate population draws from across Alliance Space
planets.economy: Incarceration services, broadcast rights, entertainment, corporate security contracts
planets.access_note: Access by contract arrangement only, media and staff credentials required. Unauthorised approach treated as hostile intrusion.
hazards: Inmate population, organised criminal networks, gang hierarchy, constant violence
Consortium security forces, well-equipped, loyal to profit not law
Broadcast zones, being filmed has legal and social consequences outside the facility
Blackmail risk, Consortium security records everything

notable_locations.name: The Facility (General Population)
notable_locations.desc: The world's largest incarceration complex. Divided into numbered sectors with varying conditions. Sector 1 is relatively comfortable. Sector 9 is where the broadcast shows are recorded.

notable_locations.name: Ridge Track (Broadcast)
notable_locations.desc: The course used for Ridge Racing, one of the galaxy's most watched programmes. Inmates participate. The degree to which this is voluntary is not discussed publicly.

notable_locations.name: Blood Bowl Arena
notable_locations.desc: Broadcast capacity 80,000. Sellout broadcast audience across Alliance Space every cycle. The Consortium considers this its flagship cultural export. Casualty rates are part of the format.

notable_locations.name: Survivor Zones
notable_locations.desc: A series of terrain environments in the planet's southern continent where Survivor is recorded. The terrain is unmodified. The conditions are unmodified. The casualty rate is part of the format.

specialties.name: Ridge Racing (Broadcast)
specialties.desc: The single most-watched sport in the galaxy: a lethal circuit race run by inmate drivers and followed by billions who mostly prefer not to think about where the drivers come from. Voran's crown jewel.

specialties.name: Ridge Racing Gear
specialties.desc: The officially branded racing gear, vehicles, suits, and parts, that rides Ridge Racing's fame onto every world that can receive the signal. A legitimate consumer empire grown straight out of a prison bloodsport.

specialties.name: Blood Bowl & Survivor
specialties.desc: The gladiatorial arena and the lethal wilderness show, the rest of Voran's prime-time slate, cast entirely from the prison population.

specialties.name: Prison-Labour Contracts
specialties.desc: Aderan's quietest export: captive inmate labour rented to industry across Alliance space at rates no free worker could survive. The sentence and the work order are the same document.

hooks: It is broadly known in Alliance political circles that the Aderan Correctional Consortium holds incarceration contracts on individuals from several powerful families, contracts placed through intermediaries that obscure the political connection. The Consortium is believed to use this knowledge as leverage in ways that never become public.

Journalists who have attempted to document conditions in the Facility's Sector 9 have a consistent record of stopping communication shortly after arrival and not being heard from again. The Consortium's explanation is always the same: the journalist chose not to file. The pattern is old enough that media organisations now consider Sector 9 assignments a one-way assignment.

It is known among information brokers in Alliance Space that the Facility on Aderan 3 houses individuals who carry significant knowledge, people who were incarcerated specifically to remove them from circulation rather than to punish a crime. The Consortium monitors all communication, which is why that knowledge has never successfully left.

Labour brokers across Alliance space know that Aderan inmate-labour contracts are priced below any legal free-labour rate, and that the time-off-sentence offered for the most dangerous work tends to expire, on paper, just before it would have freed anyone. The corporations that use the labour ask no questions, and the inmates who survive the contracts are rarely the ones who signed them.

Among Ridge Racing's enormous fanbase it is an article of faith that the drivers are willing professionals, a belief Voran spends heavily to protect. Leaked rosters listing a champion driver's conviction and sentence never circulate for long, and the few journalists who have pulled that thread have a curious habit of accepting very good jobs in Voran's media division.
planets.desc: The only surviving inhabited world in the Aderan system has found a highly profitable purpose.
