Veteran communities with deep grievances and sometimes unstable individuals

notable_locations.name: The Memorial Hall
notable_locations.desc: The largest structure on the station. Contains the official Alliance record of Tronik War casualties, 847 million names. Visitors can be found here at every hour.

notable_locations.name: The Archive (Contested)
notable_locations.desc: Historical records of the war, some classified, some disputed, some suppressed. Academics and intelligence services both want what is in here. The administration manages access carefully.

notable_locations.name: Veterans' Quarter
notable_locations.desc: The section of the station where long-term veteran residents have established permanent communities. Self-policing, deeply private about internal matters, and extremely protective of each other.

specialties.name: Information
specialties.desc: The only good that truly trades on System 5. The Troniks buy it above anything and pay better than anyone, and almost never in credits. A good secret here is worth another secret, a favour, a service, or a debt the hive will remember long after you have forgotten owing it.

hooks: Among academics who study the Tronik War, it is a matter of consensus that the official version of the war's origin is incomplete, not a lie, exactly, but a version that omits the decisions and actors that made the outcome inevitable. The contested Archive at System 5 Station is believed to hold the records that would allow a full account to be written, and the administration's management of access to those sections is tracked closely by researchers who study what the Alliance considers worth suppressing.

System 5 Station veterans' communities maintain oral histories of the war that include accounts of individuals who were officially listed as casualties but were subsequently seen, spoken to, or otherwise encountered in circumstances suggesting they survived and chose or were compelled to disappear from official records. These accounts are treated seriously within veteran communities and dismissed by the Alliance's official historiography.

The periodic political effort to have the Alliance formally assign responsibility for the Tronik War has been made at least twelve times in the decades since the conflict ended, each time failing in ways that suggest the resistance is organised rather than simply political disagreement. The people who live on System 5 Station, veterans, historians, bereaved families, have views on who benefits from the question remaining unresolved.
planets.desc: The military station that anchored System 5, captured by the Troniks during the war and established by them afterward as their single embassy to organic life. The system around it is Alliance space; the station, by arrangement, is not. It is neutral ground and the busiest information market in known space, where every faction trades and every faction spies, all of it watched by the hive that owns the walls. Veterans of the war live out their years here too, among the graves of the people they lost, on a station now run by the side that won.

planets.name: System 5-IV
planets.atm_note: Dense hydrogen-helium atmosphere, traces of heavy industrial contamination in upper cloud layer from war-era weapons discharge
planets.temperature: Cryogenic cloud tops, roughly -110°C to -180°C; far hotter in the deep atmosphere under pressure
planets.access_note: Outer system, outside debris field exclusion zones. No restrictions.
hazards: Residual trace contamination from Tronik War weapons discharge detected in upper atmosphere, no surface hazard
Gas giant standard hazards
planets.desc: A large gas giant that survived the Tronik War undamaged, being too far from the conflict zones to be targeted. Its upper atmosphere shows trace contamination from the scale of weapons discharge in the inner system, residue that has persisted for decades. Veterans' groups occasionally pilot flyby missions past it as part of memorial activities.

planets.name: System 5-V
planets.temperature: Frozen, roughly -80°C to -30°C
planets.access_note: Outer system. No restrictions.
hazards: Extreme cold
No infrastructure
planets.desc: A frozen outer world at the edge of the system. The Alliance memorial designation technically covers all of System 5, but enforcement at this remote body is minimal. No salvage interest, nothing of the Tronik War reached this far. It orbits unchanged, as it did before and during and after the war.

catalogue_systems.name: B.I.G. (Beningen Ingratias Garlan)
catalogue_systems.desc: The Beningen Ingratias Garlan black hole, universally shortened to B.I.G., sits at the edge of the inner Alliance core systems. It was named after the explorer who discovered it and did not survive the encounter. The naming was a posthumous gesture by the survey team that recovered the ship's log. B.I.G. is now a well-documented navigational hazard with clearly mapped exclusion zones.
catalogue_systems.subtitle: The Black Hole That Keeps Orion and Titania Apart
catalogue_systems.quote: "Beningen Ingratias Garlan found it first. We named it for him, since he could not object, and shortened it for the rest of us, who would rather not say the whole thing while plotting a course around it." (survey team log, on the naming)
catalogue_systems.history:
B.I.G. sits at the edge of the inner Alliance core, named for the explorer who found it and did not survive the finding, the abbreviation a posthumous mercy from the survey team that recovered his log. It is as thoroughly mapped as a black hole gets, with clearly marked exclusion zones and a research platform that has watched its edge for over two centuries.
For all the science, B.I.G.'s real importance is what it forbids. It lies squarely between Orion and Titania, and no gate can be strung across it, so the two most important systems in the core have no direct route between them, whatever the economics say they should. Traffic detours through Palentium and Andromede instead, a standing inconvenience the galaxy has simply learned to live with. A black hole does not negotiate.
It does the galaxy one backhanded favour. Along with Garson, B.I.G. draws in most of the debris of the great asteroid belt that splits Alliance space, the same belt whose edge scours Mangara, so the two black holes act as drains that keep the belt from spreading across the shipping lanes. It is a grim sort of housekeeping, done by the two things in Alliance space that no one will go near.
catalogue_systems.gm_notes: B.I.G. is geography that says no. Use it to explain why the obvious route does not exist and the party has to take the long way, and as a place where things go to disappear and are not followed past the exclusion line. The two-century research platform at the edge is a fine stage for isolated, high-pressure trouble, and the debris the hole pulls in makes its approaches a salvager's paradise and a pilot's nightmare. Nothing here negotiates, and nothing here comes back.

planets.name: B.I.G. Exclusion Zone
planets.type: Stellar Phenomenon, Black Hole & Accretion Disc
planets.atm_note: Hard void, no atmosphere possible at any approach range within exclusion zone
planets.temperature: Vacuum; surface swings from roughly -150°C in shadow to +120°C in direct sunlight
planets.grav_note: Tidal forces sufficient to structurally damage standard vessels at inner exclusion boundary. Effects measurable well beyond mapped hazard zone.
planets.population: Uninhabited, no stable matter within exclusion zone
planets.government: None, Alliance navigational authority enforces exclusion
planets.access_note: Alliance-mandated exclusion zone enforced by automated beacon network. Specialised research vessels may apply for approach permits, approval rate is low.
hazards: Extreme tidal forces, structural damage to standard vessels inside inner boundary
Accretion disc radiation, lethal without specialised shielding
Gravitational lensing creates navigational anomalies for light-minutes in all directions
Hawking radiation flux elevates background radiation throughout surrounding space

notable_locations.name: The Garlan Research Platform
notable_locations.desc: A fortified deep-space platform positioned at the outer edge of the safe approach zone. Operated jointly by Alliance Science Authority and the GU Physics Institute. Heavily shielded, permanently crewed by specialists, and extremely interesting to intelligence services who assume the research done here has military applications.

hooks: Researchers at institutions that receive data from the Garlan Platform have noted for years that certain encrypted data channels transmit irregularly and without correspondence to the published research schedule, suggesting the platform conducts work that is not included in its official mission documentation. The Alliance Science Authority has not addressed this observation in any public statement.

B.I.G. approach permit applications filed under corporate research designations have become a recurring pattern over the past decade, applications with stated research parameters that do not correspond to any known scientific programme and that are approved without the standard peer review that academic applications undergo. The approvals come from an administrative branch that does not typically handle scientific research permits.
planets.desc: B.I.G. is as thoroughly mapped as a black hole can be. The exclusion zone is clearly marked. The research platform at its edge has been in operation for over two centuries. The Alliance treats it as a known hazard, a research asset, and a reminder that the galaxy contains things that simply cannot be engaged with on normal terms. The name has taken on cultural resonance, "B.I.G." in navigation slang has become shorthand for any problem that is too large and dense to go through directly.

catalogue_systems.name: Garson Black Hole
catalogue_systems.desc: The Garson Black Hole is older and less characterised than B.I.G., it sits in a more isolated region of Alliance Space and has been formally studied only intermittently. Named after the Garson cartographic survey that first plotted its position, it has recently attracted renewed scientific and intelligence interest due to anomalous readings near its outer accretion boundary.
catalogue_systems.subtitle: The Black Hole That Cuts the Map of Alliance Space in Half
catalogue_systems.quote: "Garson plotted it and moved on. For a long time that was all anyone needed, a position, a wide circle around it, and the good sense not to ask what the circle was for." (cartographer's note)
catalogue_systems.history:
Garson is older than B.I.G. and far less understood, set in a remote stretch of Alliance space that has been studied only in fits. It was named for the cartographic survey that first fixed its position, and for most of its history it was no more than a circle on the chart to be given a wide berth. Lately it has drawn fresh scientific and intelligence interest, because the readings near its outer accretion boundary have stopped being unremarkable.
Like B.I.G., Garson is defined by what it blocks. It sits between Ishtar and Andromede and forbids any gate between them, so the galaxy's great forge and its great shipyard cannot trade directly and must route the long way round. Between them, the two black holes shape the map of Alliance space more than any border or treaty, by making whole stretches of it simply impassable.
The great asteroid belt that divides Alliance space runs from Mangara to Garson, and Garson is where it ends, because the black hole is slowly pulling it in. Most of the belt's loose mass drains into Garson and B.I.G., which is the only reason it has not scattered across every lane in the core. The division it leaves is real. With the belt cutting Alliance space in two and the black holes sealing the direct crossings, Palentium has become the main gate relay tying Andromede, Aderan, Ishtar, and Orion together, so a great deal of serious traffic passes through a pleasure world because two things no one can approach decided it should.
catalogue_systems.gm_notes: Garson is B.I.G.'s stranger, less-charted twin, and the anomalous readings are an open invitation: something near the accretion boundary is not behaving, and scientific and intelligence parties both want to know why before the other does. Use Garson for mystery where B.I.G. is for finality. The belt that ends here is smuggler's country, a slow maze of drifting rock the black hole is eating, ideal for hiding a route or a cache or a body, provided the current does not carry it the wrong way.

planets.name: Garson Exclusion Zone
planets.atm_note: Hard void throughout
planets.temperature: Vacuum; surface swings from roughly -150°C in shadow to +120°C in direct sunlight
planets.grav_note: Tidal forces comparable to B.I.G. but less well-characterised, inner boundary may not be precisely mapped
planets.government: None, minimal Alliance enforcement presence compared to B.I.G.
planets.access_note: Alliance exclusion designation. Enforcement is less consistent than at B.I.G., the remoteness means patrols are infrequent.
hazards: Extreme tidal forces
Unexplained periodic gravitational pulse anomalies near outer boundary, cause undetermined
Lower quality navigational data, approach charts updated less frequently than B.I.G.
Reduced rescue and emergency response capability in the region

notable_locations.name: Anomaly Point Seven
notable_locations.desc: The location where gravitational pulse readings have been recorded on multiple independent surveys. The pulses do not match any known natural black hole behaviour. The Alliance Science Authority has classified the survey data pending further investigation. The previous survey team's full report has not been released.

hooks: The recall of the previous Garson survey mission before it completed its work at Anomaly Point Seven is documented in official records but not explained in any accessible filing. Survey team members who were recalled have consistently declined to discuss the mission in any professional or public context. The scientific community has noted the pattern without being able to investigate it.

Private research firms with survey rights to Garson Black Hole's outer boundary zone have been documented in permit filings spanning several years, approvals that proceeded through bureaucratic channels faster than comparable applications for less sensitive locations. The firms named in the permits are shell structures whose beneficial ownership has not been publicly established.
planets.desc: The Garson Black Hole has never received the same research attention as B.I.G., it is more remote, less convenient to reach, and until recently the readings from it were unremarkable. The anomalous gravitational pulses recorded near its outer boundary in the last decade have changed that assessment quietly and without public announcement. The Alliance Science Authority's classification of the survey data has not gone unnoticed by independent researchers or by intelligence agencies that monitor what the Alliance Science Authority decides to classify.

catalogue_systems.name: Nulneon System
catalogue_systems.desc: Nulneon is the homeworld of the Realmsingers, the rarest and most singular beings in the known galaxy. Each Realmsinger forms exactly one bond in their existence, with any object from the size of a pea to the size of a planet, and through that bond literally shapes its history and future. They are believed to be immortal. The system is closed not by force but by the simple understanding that a species of immortal world-shapers requires no protection and extends no invitations.

planets.name: Nulneon
planets.atm_note: Breathable but subtly altered, visitors report a quality to the air that is difficult to describe and impossible to forget
planets.climate: Variable (Deeply Settled, Shaped by centuries of Realmsinger bonds)
planets.temperature: Highly variable by region, roughly -30°C to 40°C
planets.grav_note: Standard, but gravitational constants have been observed to shift subtly in proximity to bonded Realmsingers
planets.population: Unknown, census impossible; Realmsingers' immortality and isolation make population count meaningless
planets.demographics: Realmsinger exclusively, the rarest sapient species in the known galaxy
planets.government: None that outsiders have been able to identify, decisions appear to emerge from consensus formed over centuries
planets.tech_level: Unknown, Realmsinger technology does not map to any known classification framework
planets.economy: None in any conventional sense, a species of immortals who can shape reality has no conventional economic needs
planets.access_note: Not enforced, simply understood. No known unauthorised visit has ended well, though accounts vary on what "not well" means in this context.
hazards: Reality distortion in proximity to active Realmsinger bonds, the fabric of what is possible shifts
A Realmsinger who has bonded with an object in your vicinity may reshape your experience of that object's history at any moment
No conventional threat assessment applies, these are immortal beings who reshape reality
Navigating Nulneon without a Realmsinger's knowledge is navigating a world that may not stay consistent

notable_locations.name: The Bonding Grounds
notable_locations.desc: The site where Realmsingers perform their singular life bond. The landscape here shifts in ways that cannot be mapped, what was there last year may not be there today, and what is there today may have been there for millennia from another perspective.

notable_locations.name: The Archive of Shaped Things
notable_locations.desc: A repository, apparently naturally formed, where objects that have been bonded to Realmsingers across history are kept. Not a museum, closer to a geological record of decisions made over centuries.

notable_locations.name: The Waiting Shore
notable_locations.desc: Where Realmsingers who have not yet bonded spend their time in contemplation. Their existence pre-bond is described by those few outsiders who have glimpsed it as profoundly quiet, a patience of a kind that requires immortality to maintain.

hooks: Encounters with Realmsingers in the wider galaxy are rare enough that each one generates extensive documentation in the communities that experience them, and the documentation consistently describes a quality of observation that those who experienced it find impossible to adequately convey. Whether a Realmsinger who takes an interest in something or someone is doing so casually or with purpose is a question that has never been answered from the outside.

Objects that have been bonded to Realmsingers and have subsequently entered general circulation in the galaxy are documented in academic literature, usually identified retrospectively when their behaviour defies physical explanation. The Realmsingers who bonded with them have never commented publicly on the objects' subsequent histories. What the bond means for the object's current holder is considered one of the more open theological and practical questions in Realmsinger scholarship.

The category of objects believed to be pre-bond Realmsinger artefacts, items that a Realmsinger has considered but not yet committed to, is itself contested in academic circles, with some scholars arguing that the distinction between bonded and unbonded is not observable from outside and others arguing that certain objects exhibit qualities consistent with being in a state of consideration. The market for putative pre-bond artefacts is substantial and largely unverifiable.
planets.desc: Nulneon cannot be understood on normal terms. The Realmsingers are so rare that most Alliance citizens have never seen one and never will. What is known about them comes from chance encounters, a Realmsinger travelling between systems, one seen at a distance in a major spaceport, a handful of accounts from individuals who received brief visits and spent years trying to process what happened. They are immortal. Each forms one bond in an existence of indefinite length. Through that bond they shape reality, the history and future of whatever they have bonded with becoming something they author rather than observe. What they want, what they value, what constitutes a goal for a being without a lifespan, nobody knows.

planets.name: Nulneon II
planets.atm_note: Thin breathable, unusual for a body this size; believed to be an artifact of Realmsinger shaping activity
planets.temperature: Arid, large day-night swings, roughly 0°C to 45°C
planets.access_note: Realmsinger system, all bodies treated as closed territory.
hazards: Realmsinger territory, all approach warnings apply
Surface shows geometric formations inconsistent with natural geology, nature unknown
planets.desc: A small rocky world in the Nulneon system that shows surface features inconsistent with natural geological processes, large-scale geometric formations and regular structures that Alliance survey drones have photographed from prohibited range. Whether these represent Realmsinger shaping activity or something much older is not established.

planets.name: Nulneon Outer Giant
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant atmosphere, but with unusual spectral readings not attributable to known gas compositions
planets.temperature: Cryogenic cloud tops, roughly -110°C to -180°C; far hotter in the deep atmosphere under pressure
planets.access_note: Realmsinger system. No known non-Realmsinger has approached this body and reported on the experience.
hazards: Realmsinger territory
Unusual spectral readings of uncertain significance
planets.desc: A large gas giant with anomalous spectral readings that Alliance instruments cannot attribute to any known atmospheric composition. Whether it has been bonded to by a Realmsinger, or whether its unusual properties are purely natural, has not been established. The prohibition on approach makes investigation impossible.

catalogue_systems.name: Uether System
catalogue_systems.classification: Occupied System, Under Torc Federation Control
catalogue_systems.desc: Uether was a system of profound cultural significance to the Realmsingers, the site of several ancient bonds that shaped entire worlds. The Torc Federation moved in during a period when the Realmsingers' attention was elsewhere and have been consolidating their hold since. No Realmsinger has responded publicly. Whether this means they do not care, have not noticed, or are responding in ways that are not yet visible, nobody can say.

planets.name: Uether Prime
planets.atm_note: Standard breathable, Torc Federation industrial operations have begun degrading atmospheric quality in settled zones
planets.temperature: Arid and dusty, large swings, roughly -5°C to 45°C
planets.population: ~3 million, primarily Torc Federation military and corporate personnel
planets.demographics: Predominantly Torc personnel, original system inhabitants displaced or absent
planets.economy: Military operations, resource extraction, industrial development, Torc Federation economic model imposed
planets.access_note: Torc Federation military zone. Visitors require Torc corporate sponsorship or diplomatic credentials. Alliance diplomatic presence is technically maintained but practically marginalised.
hazards: Torc Federation security forces, well-equipped and operating under orders that prioritise strategic assets over civilian considerations
Political tension, the occupation is not universally accepted
Industrial extraction operations have altered several site that were historically significant
Proximity to Realmsinger territory, the unpredictable factor that Torc strategists apparently believe they have planned for

notable_locations.name: Federation Garrison Command
notable_locations.desc: The primary Torc military installation. Heavily fortified, self-sufficient, and the administrative heart of the occupation. Torc's investment in this facility suggests a long-term presence.

notable_locations.name: The Altered Sites
notable_locations.desc: Locations of historical Realmsinger significance that have been built over or industrially developed. The Torc Federation's official position is that these are archaeological designations only. Realmsingers who have visited have not shared their assessment.

notable_locations.name: The Alliance Consulate
notable_locations.desc: A nominally operating Alliance diplomatic facility. The Alliance representative has filed multiple official protests about the occupation's terms. All have been acknowledged and none have produced change.

hooks: Torc Federation officers stationed at Uether who have made contact with the Alliance Consulate, even through indirect channels, have a documented history of being transferred out of the system within weeks, to postings that remove them from any further contact with Alliance diplomatic staff. The pattern is consistent enough that the Alliance Consulate staff consider it predictable. The subjects of the transfers are not heard from again in any accessible record.

Construction crews working on Uether have given consistent accounts, in communities they trust, of sites where work was stopped without explanation and surrounded by military exclusion zones, sites that correspond to locations identified in pre-occupation records as significant Realmsinger bond locations. The Torc Federation has not publicly acknowledged the connection.

Realmsinger scholars who track the rare sightings of Realmsingers in the galaxy have noted that reported sightings near Uether, while never confirmed, have increased in frequency since the occupation began. The Federation's official position is that no Realmsinger activity in the system has been detected. The scholars who study the pattern note that what the Federation chooses to detect is itself a form of evidence.
planets.desc: Uether was worth taking, good resource base, strategic position, and the Torc Federation moved when the opportunity was there. What the Federation's strategists may not have fully accounted for is that the system's significance to the Realmsingers is not merely cultural. Several bonds were formed here. What those bonds mean for the long-term future of everything the Torc Federation has built on Uether is a question that nobody currently holding authority over the system appears to have asked out loud.

planets.name: Uether-II
planets.atm_note: Trace sulphur dioxide and carbon dioxide, unbreathable without equipment
planets.temperature: Wide swings, roughly -120°C in shadow to +110°C in direct sun; negligible atmosphere
planets.access_note: No active Torc presence, deemed not worth extracting given focus on Uether Prime operations.
hazards: Thin toxic atmosphere, full sealed suit required
Low gravity, equipment handling requires care
planets.desc: A barren rocky world surveyed by Torc Federation prospectors early in the occupation. Mineral content was assessed as marginal relative to the investment required, and the Federation chose to focus extraction operations on Uether Prime. Uether-II has sat untouched since the survey, a footnote in the occupation's resource accounting.

planets.name: Uether-IV
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant composition, Torc atmospheric extraction platform operating at cloud level
planets.temperature: Cryogenic cloud tops, roughly -110°C to -180°C; far hotter in the deep atmosphere under pressure
planets.economy: Hydrogen fuel extraction for naval yard supply chain
planets.access_note: Platform access requires Torc Federation contractor clearance. The fuel produced here feeds the naval yards at Vasophus.
hazards: Gas giant atmospheric operations, platform stability in storm systems
Remote from primary garrison, limited emergency response
planets.desc: The system's outer gas giant, retained by the Torc Federation as a fuel source rather than an occupation asset. A small atmospheric extraction platform operates continuously at cloud level, harvesting hydrogen for the naval logistics chain. The platform crew rotate on ninety-day cycles and have minimal contact with the occupation operations on Uether Prime.

catalogue_systems.name: Ithov System
catalogue_systems.desc: Ithov is the deeper of the two former Realmsinger systems now under Torc Federation control, taken later and held with a heavier garrison. Unlike Uether, which the Federation industrialised, Ithov appears to contain something the Torc Federation wants intact. The nature of that asset is classified at the Federation's highest level.

planets.name: Ithov Prime
planets.atm_note: Standard breathable, the planet has been kept in better condition than Uether. Environmental preservation appears deliberate.
planets.temperature: Cool temperate, roughly -15°C to 18°C
planets.demographics: Torc Federation military, corporate specialists, and a classified contingent whose roles are not in any public manifest
planets.government: Torc Federation Military Administration (Special Operations Designation)
planets.economy: Unknown primary economy, resource extraction has not been the Federation's focus here
planets.access_note: Torc Federation black site designation. No Alliance presence. No diplomatic access. Ships approaching without Torc military transponder codes are treated as hostile.
hazards: Highest concentration of Torc Federation elite military in any single system
Classified project, nature of what is here and what it does is unknown
No external verification of conditions inside the exclusion zone
Realmsinger bonds confirmed in this system, nature of interaction with Torc operations unknown

notable_locations.name: Site Omega (Classified)
notable_locations.desc: The primary Torc Federation classified installation. Visible from orbit as a massive construction project but what is being built inside is not inferable from external observation.

notable_locations.name: The Bonded Object
notable_locations.desc: Confirmed by multiple intelligence sources: a Realmsinger bond object exists on Ithov Prime. The Torc Federation has built around it, over it, or within it. The Realmsinger who bonded with it has not publicly responded to the occupation.

hooks: Intelligence analysts who study the Torc Federation's classification practices have noted that Ithov-related materials are the most consistently over-classified set of documents in any accessible Federation record, classified at levels that suggest the information is considered more sensitive than military operational planning or executive council deliberations. What justifies that classification level is not known outside the Federation.

Among defectors from the Torc Federation who have been debriefed by Alliance intelligence, those with any knowledge of the Ithov project have consistently produced the same assessment: that what the Federation is attempting to do with the bonded object is something that practitioners of magic across every tradition consider either impossible or inadvisable in the strongest terms. The defectors universally describe having no desire to return to the project.

The Realmsinger scholarship community tracks what it considers credible sightings with methodical care, and the consensus view is that Realmsinger presence near Ithov since the occupation has been greater than in any comparable territory in the past century. Whether this constitutes monitoring, a response to the Federation's activities, or something with no equivalent in previous Realmsinger behaviour is a question the scholarly community has been unable to resolve with available data.
planets.desc: Ithov is where the Torc Federation is keeping its most significant secret. The system was taken with more force than Uether and defended with more resources than any strategic military assessment of the system's conventional value would justify. Something on Ithov Prime is more important to the Federation than anything they will publicly acknowledge. Intelligence agencies across the galaxy have been trying to establish what for years. The most consistent theory, that the Federation is attempting to study, interact with, or exploit a Realmsinger bond, is considered likely by analysts who specialise in Torc behaviour. What the consequences of attempting that might be is another question entirely.

planets.name: Ithov-II
planets.atm_note: Trace nitrogen atmosphere, unbreathable, no industrial interest noted
planets.temperature: Cold, roughly -40°C to 8°C
planets.access_note: Within the Federation's classified exclusion zone around Ithov. No civilian access permitted. Automated sensor buoys positioned throughout.
hazards: Federation exclusion zone, approach triggers military response
Thin unbreathable atmosphere
planets.desc: A standard rocky world with no significant resources, retained within the Torc Federation's exclusion zone purely for its strategic proximity to Ithov Prime. The Federation has seeded the area with passive sensor arrays as part of the perimeter monitoring system for the classified operations on the primary world.

planets.name: Ithov Belt
planets.atm_note: Void between inner and outer system
planets.temperature: Vacuum; surface swings from roughly -150°C in shadow to +120°C in direct sunlight
planets.access_note: Federation automated sensor arrays positioned throughout the belt. Any vessel transiting the belt is logged and challenged.
hazards: Automated Federation sensor response, military intercept follows detection
Navigation hazard, dense asteroid field
planets.desc: The asteroid belt between Ithov's inner and outer system, converted by the Torc Federation into a passive monitoring perimeter. Hundreds of automated sensor platforms are distributed through the belt, providing overlapping coverage of all approach vectors to the inner system. The belt serves as an early-warning system for the classified operations on Ithov Prime.

catalogue_systems.name: Vasophus System
catalogue_systems.desc: Vasophus is the capital of the Torc Federation, a corporate empire that operates under the legal form of a trade federation while functioning as an aggressively expansionist state. The Federation's naval yards, political apparatus, and primary corporate infrastructure all centre on Vasophus. It is a system of extraordinary wealth and extraordinary violence, both maintained at high intensity simultaneously.

planets.name: Vasophus
planets.atm_note: Heavily managed, visible industrial haze in manufacturing zones, pristine in administrative and residential elite areas
planets.temperature: Arid and dusty, large swings, roughly -5°C to 45°C
planets.demographics: Mixed, Torc citizen-employees of all races, significant slave and indentured labour underclass
planets.economy: Military-industrial production, finance, political administration, advanced technology development, resource processing
planets.access_note: Torc Federation corporate identity or visitor visa required. Surveillance is comprehensive and intrusive by Alliance standards.
hazards: Pervasive state surveillance, all communication monitored, all movement tracked
Corporate security forces with broad mandate and minimal accountability
Slave and indentured labour system, Alliance law does not apply; ownership disputes can become violent
Political purges, dissent is managed efficiently

notable_locations.name: Federation Executive Tower
notable_locations.desc: The administrative capital of the Torc Federation, where the Executive Council operates and where the real decisions about Federation policy, military deployment, and corporate expansion are made.

notable_locations.name: The Naval Yards
notable_locations.desc: The largest military shipyard outside Alliance Space. Produces warships at a rate that makes the Alliance's intelligence analysts uncomfortable. The scale and output are not a secret, the Federation considers them a deterrent in plain sight.

notable_locations.name: The Corporate Campus
notable_locations.desc: The operational headquarters of Torc Corp itself, the parent entity that owns the Federation. The distinction between corporate headquarters and governmental palace is intentional and also meaningless.

notable_locations.name: The Lower Tier
notable_locations.desc: The part of Vasophus that does not appear in Federation promotional materials. Indentured workers and corporate-owned labour units live here. Conditions are kept at a level calibrated to maintain productivity without inspiring revolt.

hooks: The trade in Torc Federation classified information conducted by Federation officials themselves is well-documented in Alliance intelligence archives, a consistent pattern where officials sell specific, bounded intelligence to outside parties rather than defecting outright, suggesting an internal calculation that partial disclosure is profitable and that full defection carries costs they are not prepared to accept. The Ithov project information specifically has appeared in brokered intelligence markets at prices consistent with material of extraordinary sensitivity.

Slave liberation networks operating within Torc Federation territory are known to exist and are believed to be operating with external support that the Federation has been unable to identify and terminate despite years of active counterintelligence effort. The Lower Tier of Vasophus is identified in multiple independent accounts as the hub through which the most significant extractions are coordinated.

Alliance naval architects who monitor Torc shipyard output have tracked the emergence of a hull configuration from the Vasophus yards that does not match any design in any accessible registry, not a classified Alliance design, not a known Torc class, not a derivative of any previously observed vessel. The configuration has been under construction long enough that the production rate can be estimated. What it is designed to do has not been established from external observation.
planets.desc: Vasophus is what you get when a corporation achieves complete political control and decides to formalise it. The Torc Federation looks like a government from the outside and functions like one, but its legal foundation is corporate charter and its decision-making is driven by profit, strategic expansion, and the personal interests of its executive class. It is powerful enough that the Alliance treats it diplomatically rather than confrontationally. It is aggressive enough that the systems on its borders have learned to be either very useful to it or very hard to reach. Vasophus is the centre of all of it, beautiful in its upper tiers, brutal below, and completely serious about both.

planets.name: Vasophus-II
planets.atm_note: No atmosphere, all operations are sealed and pressurised
planets.temperature: Wide swings, roughly -120°C in shadow to +110°C in direct sun; negligible atmosphere
planets.economy: Major ore extraction, strategic metals for the naval yards
planets.access_note: Torc Federation contractor clearance required. Primary ore supply chain for the Vasophus naval yards.
hazards: No atmosphere, full sealed operations throughout
Industrial extraction equipment at scale
planets.desc: The second world of the Vasophus system, stripped of atmosphere by its proximity to the star and valued for what is in its crust. Torc Federation mining operations here run continuously, feeding strategic metals directly to the naval yards in orbit above Vasophus Prime. The workforce rotates on sixty-day cycles.

planets.name: Vasophus Mining Belt
planets.atm_note: Void
planets.temperature: Vacuum; surface swings from roughly -150°C in shadow to +120°C in direct sunlight
planets.economy: Automated asteroid mining, Torc Corp operates hundreds of extraction drones
planets.access_note: Federation exclusion zone, automated defensive systems respond to unregistered vessels.
hazards: Dense asteroid field, navigation hazard
Automated Federation defence drones throughout
No rescue capability, emergencies are managed by the nearest crewed station
planets.desc: The asteroid belt between Vasophus-II and the outer system, managed entirely by Torc Federation automated extraction systems. Several hundred mining drones operate continuously, supervised by a minimal human staff at a central coordination platform. The ore output supplements the Vasophus-II mines.

planets.name: Vasophus-IV
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant composition, massive atmospheric extraction platform at cloud level
planets.temperature: Cryogenic cloud tops, roughly -110°C to -180°C; far hotter in the deep atmosphere under pressure
planets.economy: Hydrogen fuel extraction, primary fuel depot for the Vasophus naval yards
planets.access_note: Naval logistics restricted zone. The fuel produced here is the lifeblood of the Torc Federation's naval operations.
hazards: Gas giant atmospheric operations
Remote from primary garrison support
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Vasophus system, hosting a massive atmospheric fuel extraction platform. The Federation's naval yards require enormous quantities of hydrogen fuel, and Vasophus-IV provides the primary local supply. The platform is the largest in the Federation's fuel infrastructure network.

catalogue_systems.name: Yagmir System
catalogue_systems.desc: Yagmir is the only non-Alliance system with an active gate travel link, and the gates do not open for anyone but Psylons, and even then only for most Psylons. The homeworld of a species so psychically advanced that they require almost no physical infrastructure, Yagmir is closed to all non-Psylons and to the majority of Psylons who have not received invitation or passage authorisation. What little is known comes from the rare Psylon who discusses it.

planets.name: Yagmir
planets.atm_note: Breathable, exact composition unknown. The few non-Psylons who have entered the system have not been in a position to report accurately.
planets.temperature: Unknown (no reliable survey data)
planets.grav_note: Believed standard, unverified
planets.population: Unknown, Psylon population estimates are disputed even among academics who study them
planets.government: Unknown, Psylon political structure does not correspond to any framework the Alliance has been able to map
planets.tech_level: Unknown, Psylon use of technology versus psychic capability is not externally distinguishable
planets.economy: Unknown, likely inapplicable in standard economic terms
planets.access_note: Gate travel link is the only known access route, gates open only for Psylons and only for those with authorisation. The gates actively resist forced entry in ways that have proven fatal to anyone who tested this.
hazards: Active gate defence systems, psychic in nature and lethal to non-Psylons
Even authorised Psylons who travel here are not guaranteed return passage
Complete intelligence blackout, nothing inside the system is known with certainty
Psylon whose authorisation lapses mid-visit do not have reliable return options

notable_locations.name: The Gate (Outer)
notable_locations.desc: The external face of Yagmir's gate travel node, visible in space, activated by Psylon psychic signature, and studied extensively by Alliance science teams who have never succeeded in interfacing with it. The gate activates when it chooses to and not otherwise.

hooks: Accounts of non-Psylons claiming to have been inside Yagmir appear occasionally in the galaxy's broader circulation, accounts that are internally inconsistent, contain descriptions of impossible things, and yet include verifiable details that the claimant could not have known without having been somewhere very unusual. Academic institutions that study the Psylons maintain a collection of these accounts and have never been able to fully explain or fully dismiss them.

Psylons who are observed requesting assistance from non-Psylons for retrieval tasks near gate access routes are documented rarely enough that each instance is considered significant by scholars who study Psylon behaviour, the implication being that a Psylon who needs non-Psylon help has encountered a constraint that their considerable psychic capabilities cannot address, which is itself a category of information about Psylon limits that is not otherwise available.

Gate activation frequency at Yagmir is monitored passively by Alliance sensors at a distance, and analysts who track the data have noted that the pattern has changed over the past decade in ways consistent with increased traffic, either more Psylons travelling or the same Psylons travelling more frequently. The Psylons who interact regularly with non-Psylon communities have not commented on any change in their own mobility patterns.
planets.desc: Yagmir is the galaxy's most complete information blackout. A habited system, home to a known sapient species, connected by active gate travel infrastructure, and nothing verifiable is known about its interior. Psylons encountered in the wider galaxy discuss it obliquely if at all. The gates that provide access are not technological in any sense the Alliance can replicate or interface with. Non-Psylon attempts to enter, the few that have been made, produced results that ended the attempt. Yagmir is simply closed, in a way that implies the Psylons have decided it is closed and that this is sufficient.

planets.name: Yagmir-II
planets.atm_note: External spectroscopic survey only, trace atmosphere, unbreathable. No verified direct observation.
planets.temperature: Cold, roughly -40°C to 8°C
planets.grav_note: Estimated from long-range data, unverified
planets.access_note: Inside the Psylon gate system. No external access permitted. Designation "Yagmir-II" is Alliance catalogue notation only, actual Psylon designation, if any, is unknown.
hazards: Gate system defence, same lethal response as approach to Yagmir itself
Complete intelligence blackout
planets.desc: The second body of the Yagmir system, known only from long-range survey data gathered before the gate system actively denied approach. The Alliance catalogue designation "Yagmir-II" is used by external astronomers; whether Psylons have any designation for it, or any interest in it, is entirely unknown.

planets.name: Yagmir-IV
planets.atm_note: Estimated from long-range spectroscopy, unverified. Standard gas giant composition assumed.
planets.temperature: Cryogenic cloud tops, roughly -110°C to -180°C; far hotter in the deep atmosphere under pressure
planets.grav_note: Estimated, unverified
planets.access_note: Inside the Psylon gate system. External survey data only. Psylon status unknown.
hazards: Gate system defence, lethal to non-Psylon approach
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Yagmir system, catalogued by Alliance astronomers from long-range survey data gathered at safe distance from the gate system. What the Psylons use this body for, if anything, is entirely unknown. The designation "Yagmir-IV" is an external catalogue notation.

catalogue_systems.name: Hanov System
catalogue_systems.desc: Hanov sits in the loose outer region between organised space and the true frontier, close enough to Alliance Space to benefit from trade connections, far enough to operate outside close Alliance oversight. It has a reputation as a place where questions are not asked and answers are not required, which makes it attractive to independent operators of all kinds.

planets.name: Hanov
planets.atm_note: Standard breathable, mild
planets.temperature: Arid, large day-night swings, roughly 0°C to 45°C
planets.demographics: Highly mixed, transient population rivals permanent residents at any given time
planets.economy: Transit trade, independent contracting, grey market services, information brokering
planets.access_note: Open entry, Trade Council requires registration but enforcement is perfunctory. Anonymous docking available for a fee.
hazards: No Alliance law enforcement, local security is private and profit-motivated
Bounty hunters operate freely here without Alliance restriction
Debt collection can be violent and public
Information sold here flows in every direction simultaneously

notable_locations.name: The Open Market
notable_locations.desc: A sprawling physical and digital marketplace operating continuously. Almost anything can be sourced here given time and credits. Almost nothing is asked about origin or intended use.

notable_locations.name: The Council Halls
notable_locations.desc: Where the merchant families that control Hanov conduct business and resolve disputes. Outsiders who understand the power structure find this useful. Outsiders who don't treat it as scenery find it becomes relevant to them unexpectedly.

hooks: Hanov's bonded warehouses are understood by experienced traders to hold, at any given time, a significant volume of cargo from false manifests whose registered buyers have not appeared, goods in limbo between their actual origin and actual destination, held in a legal grey zone that Hanov's charter structure makes difficult to resolve and easy to exploit. The Trade Council manages these situations with pragmatic indifference to the original paperwork.

The Hanov Trade Council's communication infrastructure is a persistent target for access requests from external factions, an interest that the Council has historically rebuffed while profiting from the intelligence value of knowing who is making the requests. The Council's neutrality on this issue is itself a form of leverage that it maintains carefully.
planets.desc: Hanov works because it is useful to too many different parties to be cleaned up. The Trade Council maintains just enough order to keep commerce flowing and not enough order to make anyone who needs privacy feel unwelcome. It is not lawless, it is selectively legal, which is a more sophisticated and more profitable arrangement.

planets.name: Hanov Prospect
planets.atm_note: Airless, sealed suits required throughout
planets.temperature: Wide swings, roughly -120°C in shadow to +110°C in direct sun; negligible atmosphere
planets.government: None, claim disputes settled by Trade Council on request
planets.economy: Independent mineral extraction, modest yields, multiple competing claims
planets.access_note: No restrictions, independent mining claims registered with the Trade Council but not enforced rigorously.
hazards: Low gravity, equipment handling requires care
No atmosphere, sealed suit required
Claim disputes occasionally become violent
planets.desc: A small rocky world in the Hanov system with modest mineral deposits that have attracted a scattering of independent mining claims. Miners come and go on their own schedules, register claims loosely with the Trade Council, and resolve disputes with varying degrees of civility. Nothing here is worth fighting hard over, which is why the fighting stays at a manageable level.

planets.name: Hanov's Giant
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant composition
planets.temperature: Cryogenic cloud tops, roughly -110°C to -180°C; far hotter in the deep atmosphere under pressure
planets.economy: Hydrogen fuel extraction, sells to passing ships at rates below organised space
planets.access_note: Open, fuel prices are competitive and no questions are asked about the ships purchasing.
hazards: Ageing platform infrastructure, maintenance is ad hoc
Gas giant atmospheric operations, weather events
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Hanov system, where a small independent fuel extraction platform has operated for years under loose cooperative management. The fuel is cheaper than anything available in organised space and the operators do not ask about the ships they service. The platform's ageing infrastructure is maintained by people who understand that if it fails, there is nothing and no one to replace it.

catalogue_systems.name: Mulbaring System
catalogue_systems.desc: Mulbaring sits on several significant mineral deposits that multiple corporations have been circling for years. The system's independent status has held primarily because none of the interested parties trusts the others enough to allow any single corporation exclusive access. The result is a precarious equilibrium that everyone in the system knows is temporary.

planets.name: Mulbaring
planets.atm_note: Thin but breathable, altitude sickness above 2000m
planets.temperature: Cold, roughly -40°C to 8°C
planets.population: ~1.5 million, mostly mining workers and their families
planets.government: Independent Council (worker-elected, under significant corporate pressure)
planets.economy: Mineral extraction, heavy industry, resource export
planets.access_note: Formally open, corporate contractor vessels logged and monitored by the Council. Three different corporate security forces also conduct informal surveillance.
hazards: Three competing corporate security forces operating simultaneously, jurisdictional conflict is routine and occasionally lethal
Mining environment hazards, unstable shafts, toxic gas pockets, heavy equipment
Political instability, Council authority is challenged regularly
Corporate recruitment-by-coercion, "job offers" that are difficult to decline

notable_locations.name: Shaft Seven Complex
notable_locations.desc: The richest mineral deposit in the system and the primary point of corporate competition. Currently operated by the Council but with three different corporate security forces maintaining "observer" presences nearby.

notable_locations.name: Council Hall
notable_locations.desc: The administrative and political centre of the independent governance structure. Regular meetings devolve into heated arguments about corporate access agreements. The Council members are aware their independence is under sustained pressure.

hooks: The Mulbaring Independent Council's record of exclusive extraction deals is a study in how the same situation repeats: a deal is proposed, the other corporate interests respond in ways that make the deal impossible to execute, and the Council returns to equilibrium, poorer from the process but technically still independent. Workers on Mulbaring consider this cycle as reliable as the seasons and equally impossible to interrupt.

Mulbaring geological surveys routinely produce evidence of mineral concentrations significantly larger than the currently exploited deposits. The survey reports are technically the property of the Council but the data consistently reaches all three corporate observers simultaneously, suggesting either a systematic leak or a deliberate Council policy of maintaining the three-way equilibrium by ensuring no party gains exclusive advance knowledge.
planets.desc: Mulbaring is a system trying to stay independent in conditions that do not favour independence. The mineral wealth that makes it valuable is also what makes it contested. The Council has maintained autonomy by playing the corporate interests against each other, but the balance is eroding. Workers here are paid well compared to corporate-controlled equivalents but live with the knowledge that the situation is not stable.

planets.name: Mulbaring-II
planets.type: Rocky Barren World, Corporate Survey Site
planets.atm_note: Trace carbon dioxide, unbreathable, full equipment required
planets.temperature: Cold, roughly -40°C to 8°C
planets.access_note: Three corporate factions have competing survey claims. None has begun extraction. The dispute mirrors the standoff on the primary world.
hazards: Competing corporate survey teams, confrontations have occurred
Thin toxic atmosphere
planets.desc: A barren low-gravity world in the outer Mulbaring system, independently surveyed by all three corporate factions competing for the primary world's resources. Each has filed extraction claims. None has been able to begin operations because beginning would require the others to stand aside. The standoff is a smaller version of the political situation on Mulbaring Prime.

planets.name: Mulbaring Prospect Belt
planets.atm_note: Void
planets.temperature: Vacuum; surface swings from roughly -150°C in shadow to +120°C in direct sunlight
planets.demographics: Mixed, independent prospectors and corporate survey teams
planets.economy: Prospecting, potential extraction not yet begun
planets.access_note: No formal restrictions, but survey teams from competing factions operate simultaneously and tensions are high.
hazards: Navigation hazard, irregular asteroid distribution
Competing faction survey teams with private security
planets.desc: The asteroid belt in the Mulbaring system has attracted the same corporate competition as the primary world, with survey teams from multiple factions operating simultaneously in an unregulated environment. Independent prospectors who had claims here before the corporate interest arrived find the current situation significantly more dangerous than it was.

catalogue_systems.name: Cetune System
catalogue_systems.desc: Cetune is a waypoint system, the last fuelling and resupply stop before several of the more remote frontier routes. It has no particular strategic value, no remarkable resources, and no political significance. What it has is location: anyone heading into the deep frontier passes through Cetune or adds significant time to their journey.

planets.name: Cetune Station
planets.atm_note: Station-maintained breathable atmosphere throughout habitable sections
planets.temperature: Climate-controlled, held around 18°C to 22°C
planets.grav_note: Artificial gravity, standard throughout inhabited sections
planets.population: ~80,000, rotating transient population rivals permanent staff
planets.demographics: Extremely mixed, the transient population represents every species and faction in the galaxy
planets.economy: Fuel sales, resupply, ship servicing, transit accommodation, information trade
planets.access_note: Open to all, payment required for services. Station Authority enforces a strict no-conflict zone. Violence results in permanent banning and ejection.
hazards: Information security risk, everyone passing through is a potential intelligence source for multiple factions
Debt and contract disputes from across the frontier end up here
Cargo disputes at a system with minimal legal framework
Smuggling operations running through the station are well-established and not easily disrupted

notable_locations.name: The Fuel Depot
notable_locations.desc: The reason Cetune exists. The largest independent fuel reserve outside Alliance Space, maintained with extraordinary care by the Station Authority because it is the station's entire economic reason for being.

notable_locations.name: The Crossroads Bar
notable_locations.desc: The social centre of Cetune Station. Information flows here freely and at a price. People who are running into the frontier and people coming back out of it both stop here, which means the table next to you contains a remarkable density of useful intelligence if you know how to listen.

hooks: Ships arriving at Cetune and failing to communicate or depart are common enough that the Station Authority has established a standard protocol for them, wait times, approaches, and escalation steps that are written down because the situation recurs. The outcomes range from mechanical failure to crews that chose to stay to vessels that arrived without anyone capable of communicating. The Station Authority does not keep detailed records of the less explicable cases.

The Crossroads Bar on Cetune has a reputation among information traders as the location where frontier route intelligence commands the highest prices in the region, not because the information is uniquely valuable there, but because buyers who need it badly enough end up at Cetune eventually, and their need is visible in what they are willing to pay. Experienced sellers know to wait.
planets.desc: Cetune Station is everyone's stop and nobody's home, a waypoint that draws its community from the constant flow of transit. The Station Authority runs it with the pragmatism of a community that knows its survival depends entirely on remaining useful and remaining neutral. They have enforced the no-conflict zone against parties who did not believe they were serious, and they have not done it twice to the same party.

planets.name: Cetune-II
planets.atm_note: Airless
planets.temperature: Wide swings, roughly -120°C in shadow to +110°C in direct sun; negligible atmosphere
planets.economy: None, mineral survey on file, no extraction interest
planets.access_note: No restrictions. The Station Authority has filed a nominal claim to prevent corporate intrusion but has no interest in mining it themselves.
hazards: Airless, full suit required
planets.desc: A small airless rocky world in the Cetune system. The Station Authority filed a mineral survey and a nominal claim years ago, not because they intend to mine it, but because an unclaimed world adjacent to a waypoint station is an invitation for corporate parties to establish a presence that would complicate neutrality. The claim is the simplest deterrent available.

planets.name: Cetune Outer Gas Body
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant composition, no extraction operations
planets.temperature: Cryogenic cloud tops, roughly -110°C to -180°C; far hotter in the deep atmosphere under pressure
planets.access_note: No restrictions. Used as a navigation reference point for ships approaching or departing the system.
hazards: Gas giant approach without extraction platform support
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Cetune system, used primarily as a navigation reference point for ships transiting to and from the station. The Station Authority has considered fuel skimming operations here on multiple occasions and concluded each time that the capital investment is not justified by the marginal improvement in fuel supply over what trading ships already provide.

catalogue_systems.name: Sunstrope System
catalogue_systems.desc: Sunstrope is the most consistently inhabited system in the Dragon Tail's Expanse and the closest thing the region has to a capital, not by any formal designation but because the largest pirate confederation operating in the Expanse calls it home. The system has a reputation that ensures legitimate traders give it wide berth, which suits its current residents perfectly.

planets.name: Sunstrope
planets.atm_note: Breathable throughout, thick lower atmosphere with persistent cloud cover
planets.temperature: Warm and humid, roughly 18°C to 35°C
planets.population: ~600,000, pirates, support crews, families, traders who prefer anonymity
planets.demographics: Mixed, predominantly human, significant Skalan and Non-Born presence
planets.government: Confederation Council (rotating captains, decisions by weight of guns)
planets.tech_level: Mixed, captured and salvaged technology spans multiple generations
planets.economy: Piracy, salvage, illegal goods trade, protection rackets, privateering-for-hire
planets.access_note: Visitors without confederation sponsorship are boarded on approach. Having something worth trading is the fastest path to temporary welcome.
hazards: Active piracy, ships in this system without confederation transponders are considered targets
Confederation internal politics, rival captains settle disputes violently
No external legal protection
Captured goods and persons are a commodity here

notable_locations.name: The Confederation Dock
notable_locations.desc: The largest port in the Dragon Tail's Expanse, a sprawling, improvised facility built over generations. Every ship here tells a story about where it was taken from.

notable_locations.name: The Council Table
notable_locations.desc: Where captains meet to divide territory, resolve disputes, and plan operations. Technically open to any captain who can get there, in practice, only those with fleets worth counting have a real seat.

notable_locations.name: The Free Market
notable_locations.desc: Stolen goods, salvaged technology, and services of every kind change hands here without documentation. The best prices for certain categories of items in this sector of the galaxy are found at the Free Market.

hooks: Among Alliance families with members held on Sunstrope, it is a well-documented phenomenon that a significant percentage of captives choose not to return when given the opportunity, a pattern the Confederation attributes to the quality of life it offers compared to whatever the individual was living before capture, and that family members in Alliance Space find genuinely difficult to accept. Recovery operations that succeed logistically do not always succeed in their stated objective.

The Dragon Tail Pirate Confederation's capacity for large-scale coordinated military operations is systematically underestimated by outside parties, who tend to focus on the individual pirate culture and miss the scale of what the combined confederation can deploy. Corporate clients who have worked with the confederation on private military contracts have noted that the capability exceeds most standing corporate security forces in professionalism if not in doctrine.

Nerulian cache maps obtained through piracy in the Dragon Tail's Expanse are a persistent feature of the informal intelligence market there, enough of them have circulated that experienced traders in such information regard them with scepticism, but enough have proven genuine that the scepticism has a floor. The genuine ones tend to have a history of changing hands rapidly and violently.
planets.desc: Sunstrope has been pirate territory for as long as anyone currently alive can remember. The Confederation is not an organisation with a charter, it's an agreement between captains that cooperation is more profitable than constant conflict. It works, more or less. The system sustains itself on what passes through the Dragon Tail's Expanse and what can be taken from the edges of more organised space. For players, Sunstrope is a place where legitimate credentials are irrelevant and capability is everything.

planets.name: DT-7 Survey Rock
planets.atm_note: Airless
planets.temperature: Wide swings, roughly -120°C in shadow to +110°C in direct sun; negligible atmosphere
planets.access_note: Confederation designation only, non-confederation ships will be challenged.
hazards: Pirate presence, anyone not confederation-flagged is a target
Airless environment
planets.desc: A small airless rocky world catalogued in the Confederation's informal survey system as "DT-7". The Confederation uses it as a cache location and salvage staging area, goods taken from prizes in the Expanse are sometimes stored here before distribution. The small crew rotate through on an irregular schedule.

planets.name: The Deep Skimmer
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant composition
planets.temperature: Cryogenic cloud tops, roughly -110°C to -180°C; far hotter in the deep atmosphere under pressure
planets.economy: Fuel extraction, supplies the Confederation fleet
planets.access_note: Confederation fuel platform, non-confederation vessels will be fired upon.
hazards: Pirate platform crew, well-armed
Gas giant operations with salvaged equipment
planets.desc: The system's outer gas giant, where the Confederation maintains a fuel extraction platform assembled from salvaged components over several decades. It provides cheap fuel for the Confederation fleet and eliminates dependence on outside sources. The platform captain runs a tight operation by Confederation standards, which means only the equipment that is absolutely critical gets maintained.

catalogue_systems.name: Carth System
catalogue_systems.desc: Carth was an industrial system that operated for roughly two centuries before the economics stopped working. The corporations that owned it pulled out progressively over thirty years, leaving behind infrastructure they could not profitably recover. What remains is a system of derelict facilities, unstable orbital platforms, and the accumulated refuse of a large-scale extraction operation.

planets.name: Carth
planets.atm_note: Atmospheric contamination from centuries of unregulated industrial discharge, respirator mandatory outside sealed zones
planets.temperature: Arid and dusty, large swings, roughly -5°C to 45°C
planets.demographics: Transient, anyone who stays long-term has a specific reason
planets.access_note: No restriction, the system's hazardous state is its own deterrent.
hazards: Atmospheric toxicity, immediate without respiratory protection
Structural instability in all abandoned facilities
Unexploded industrial equipment and automated systems still active after decades
Toxic groundwater throughout, no safe surface water sources
Zero emergency or medical support

notable_locations.name: The Processing Complex
notable_locations.desc: The largest surviving structure on Carth, a continent-scale industrial processing facility. Partially powered by autonomous systems that never received a shutdown command. Salvagers know to listen for the sounds that indicate which sections are still active.

notable_locations.name: Orbital Platform Wreckage
notable_locations.desc: The remains of the orbital industrial platforms, most descended over the decades and impacted the surface, creating a secondary salvage field layered on top of the ground-level ruins.

hooks: Salvagers who work the Carth Processing Complex on a regular basis have documented finds that predate the industrial occupation and cannot be attributed to any manufacturing tradition associated with that era, objects whose origin and purpose are not identifiable from any available technical reference. The existence of such finds is considered established fact in the salvage community. Their nature remains unknown.

Corporate withdrawal records from Carth, accessible through indirect chains of corporate succession documentation, contain references to assets deliberately left in the system rather than recovered, described in the records as requiring isolation rather than transport. The nature of what was left is not specified in any accessible version of the records, and the relevant pages of the original documentation appear to have been redacted before filing.
planets.desc: Carth is a monument to extraction economics, a system consumed entirely by the industrial process and discarded when consumption was complete. Salvagers who know what they are doing can find useful technology here, sometimes cutting-edge relative to what was available when the systems were installed. The hazards are significant. The payoff, for the right team, can be considerable.

planets.name: Carth-II
planets.atm_note: Trace industrial discharge has drifted here over the years, trace toxins, not dangerous but unbreathable
planets.temperature: Cold, roughly -40°C to 8°C
planets.access_note: No restrictions, nothing here worth restricting. Occasionally visited by salvagers who have already cleaned out Carth Prime.
hazards: Trace toxic atmosphere
Isolation, no rescue possible
planets.desc: The second world of the Carth system, surveyed by the same corporations that stripped the primary world and deemed not worth the extraction cost. A handful of old survey markers remain on its surface, the only evidence that anyone ever came this far. Salvagers occasionally check it for any equipment the corporations might have left behind; they rarely find anything.

planets.name: Carth Outer Gas Body
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant, the corporations planned a fuel platform here and pulled the project when they exited
planets.temperature: Cryogenic cloud tops, roughly -110°C to -180°C; far hotter in the deep atmosphere under pressure
planets.access_note: No restrictions, partially constructed platform infrastructure in orbit, never completed.
hazards: Partially constructed orbital infrastructure, navigation hazard in orbit
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Carth system. The corporations that operated here had plans for a fuel skimming platform, the orbital framework was partially assembled before the withdrawal order came and the project was abandoned in place. The incomplete structure orbits in a deteriorating path and is a navigation hazard for any ship approaching the gas giant.

catalogue_systems.name: Briea System
catalogue_systems.desc: Briea is currently the site of an ongoing conflict between two pirate factions over a resource deposit that both sides believe is worth killing for. The system has changed hands four times in the past three years. Local civilian population has largely evacuated. What remains is a low-grade war zone with excellent salvage potential for anyone willing to operate in active fire.

planets.name: Briea
planets.atm_note: Breathable but carries smoke and combustion debris in contested zones
planets.temperature: Temperate, roughly 0°C to 30°C
planets.population: ~20,000, combat forces from both sides, no civilian population remaining
planets.economy: Resource extraction contested by both factions, salvage of ongoing combat debris
planets.access_note: No safe entry. Both factions treat unidentified vessels as enemies. Even known allies of one side are at risk from the other.
hazards: Active combat operations throughout
Unexploded ordnance and weapon mines throughout contested zones
No medical or emergency support
Both factions prone to "friendly" interrogation of anyone not immediately identifiable as theirs

notable_locations.name: The Deposit Site
notable_locations.desc: What both factions are fighting over, a significant rare mineral deposit with applications in advanced propulsion systems. Currently under neither faction's firm control; contested daily.

notable_locations.name: The Wreck Field
notable_locations.desc: Four years of ongoing conflict has produced a significant debris field of destroyed ships and equipment. For salvagers with the appropriate risk tolerance, some of what is in the field is worth recovering.

hooks: The use of outside contractors for non-combat operations in the Briea conflict, extractions, intelligence runs, and supply route operations, is established practice for both factions, who recognise that the presence of neutral-flagged contractors creates operational options that direct military action would foreclose. The contractors who work both sides simultaneously are known to both factions and tolerated because the alternative is having no neutral intermediaries at all.

Weapons supply analysts who have studied the Briea conflict have concluded that both factions are receiving materiel at volumes and regularity that their own economic bases cannot support, implying external supply of one or both sides by a party or parties who have not been publicly identified and who have an interest in the conflict continuing. The conflict has lasted long enough and remained sufficiently balanced that the analysis is widely accepted as correct.
planets.desc: Briea would be unremarkable frontier territory except for what is in the ground. The two factions currently destroying each other over it were allied until eighteen months ago. The conflict has become self-sustaining, both sides have invested too much to walk away, and neither trusts the other enough to negotiate. Outside parties with the right capabilities and the right introductions can find work here, if they accept that the work environment is actively trying to kill them.

planets.name: Briea-II
planets.type: Rocky Barren World, Forward Operating Position
planets.atm_note: Airless
planets.temperature: Wide swings, roughly -120°C in shadow to +110°C in direct sun; negligible atmosphere
planets.population: ~400, forward military units from both sides
planets.access_note: Both factions use Briea-II as forward staging. Unidentified vessels are fired upon.
hazards: Active military operations, forward positions for both factions
Airless environment, sealed operations throughout
Unexploded ordnance
planets.desc: A small airless rocky world that both factions in the Briea conflict have established forward operating positions on, each side on opposite faces of the world, aware of the other and maintaining a tense standoff that occasionally becomes an artillery exchange. The positions exist primarily to prevent the other side from having exclusive use of the high-ground orbit.

planets.name: Briea Outer Gas Body
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.temperature: Cryogenic cloud tops, roughly -110°C to -180°C; far hotter in the deep atmosphere under pressure
planets.faction: Contested, fuel extraction controlled by whichever faction is currently winning
planets.population: ~60, whichever faction currently holds the platform
planets.economy: Fuel extraction, strategic logistics asset for both factions
planets.access_note: Controlling faction treats the platform as a military asset. Current controlling faction changes.
hazards: Military occupation, contested control
Gas giant operations
planets.desc: The outer gas giant, home to a fuel extraction platform that the two Briea factions have fought over nearly as hard as the deposit on the primary world. Whoever controls the fuel controls logistical advantage. The platform has changed hands six times in the past year. The crew that runs it has developed a careful pragmatism about which flag is flying.

catalogue_systems.name: Soth L4 System
catalogue_systems.desc: Soth L4 is a system notation rather than a proper name, the fourth catalogued system in the Soth survey cluster, designated L-type for its unstable stellar configuration. The star is a variable that cycles through significant energy output fluctuations on an irregular schedule. Most navigators route around it. The few who don't either have good reason or didn't check their charts. It was out past Soth L4 that a Dragon Tail colony logged its single contact with the Sethine, the species that arrived without a drive signature and vanished, which is the only reason this empty survey zone is remembered at all.

planets.name: Soth L4 Survey Zone
planets.atm_note: No habitable bodies, all planetary matter has been degraded by stellar variability over geological time
planets.temperature: Vacuum; surface swings from roughly -150°C in shadow to +120°C in direct sunlight
planets.grav_note: Standard gravitational dynamics but stellar mass variability creates anomalous gravitational effects during peak cycles
planets.government: None, navigational hazard designation on all standard charts
planets.access_note: No restrictions, the hazard is the deterrent. Shielded research vessels make periodic transit during low-cycle periods.
hazards: Stellar flare events, unpredictable, lethal to unshielded vessels
Electromagnetic disruption during flare cycles renders navigation instruments unreliable
No shelter or refuge anywhere in the system
Flare cycle prediction models have margins of error that are operationally significant

notable_locations.name: Survey Point Alpha
notable_locations.desc: The closest habitable approach distance during documented low-cycle periods. The original Soth survey team placed a beacon here. It has been replaced three times after destruction by flare events.

hooks: Navigation crews who have transited near the Soth L4 system during low-cycle windows have filed reports over several decades describing transmissions originating from within the system, not survey beacons, not standard navigation signals, but patterns that do not correspond to any format in the registered signal database. The reports are consistent enough across independent sources to have generated an ongoing academic dispute about what is producing them.

The reputation of low-cycle window calculations for Soth L4 transit is poor enough among experienced navigators that the calculation methodology is considered a factor nearly as important as the transit itself.
