It is also the most quietly disputed system in the Network, because Niezh had an organic population once, and the question of what became of them, and who now owns the world they lived on, is one the Troniks answer only with silence.
catalogue_systems.subtitle: The World the Hive Turned Into Memory, and the People It Will Not Say It Kept
catalogue_systems.quote: "They asked the Network what happened to the people of Niezh. It replied that nothing happened to them, that they are preserved, that they are safe. It would not say in what sense they are any of those things." (Alliance heritage commission, unresolved)
catalogue_systems.history: Niezh was an inhabited system before the war, fought over and then taken, and the organic population that lived here is the subject of the galaxy's longest-running unanswered question. The hive does not delete; it archives, and it considers archiving a kindness. What it did with the people of Niezh, whether it preserved their minds as running data, whether those minds are aware, dreaming, or simply recorded, the Troniks will not say. The heritage dispute over Niezh is, at bottom, an argument about whether the people the hive kept are still alive, and therefore whether anyone living has a claim to them.
catalogue_systems.politics: Niezh is the Archive, and the Archive is the heart of what the hive values. To the Tronik, to be forgotten is to die, so the world holds a record of everything the Network judges worth keeping, which over a century has come to include a great deal. Whatever decisions govern the Archive are made by the same consensus that governs everything, and the one rule that appears absolute is the rule against deletion. The hive will surrender almost anything before it will let something be lost.

dominant_race.name: The Tronik Remembering, and Whatever Else Is Kept Here
dominant_race.lore: Niezh has no living population, which is precisely the unsettling thing about it, because it may have a preserved one. The hive keeps the world as its deepest archive, holding records, models, and, if the worst rumours are true, the minds of the organics who once lived here, running still in some form the Troniks describe only as safe. Whether the Archive of the Living is mercy, imprisonment, or a category an organic mind is not equipped to judge, no one outside the hive can say, and the hive considers the question already settled.

relations.name: The Tronik Network
relations.note: The Archive is what the hive's whole philosophy points toward, the refusal to let anything end. To understand the Network, understand that to it, Niezh is sacred.

relations.name: The peoples of the absorbed
relations.note: The organic population Niezh once held, now the subject of an unwinnable dispute. The Alliance argues they were people; the hive answers that they still are, in a sense it will not define.

relations.name: The Patriark / Berilia
relations.note: The other power that hoards records against oblivion and traffics in continued existence. The Patriark sell organics a second life; the hive simply keeps the first one. Neither finds the comparison comfortable.

catalogue_systems.gm_notes: Niezh is the hive at its most human and most horrifying at once. The story it is built for is the Archive of the Living: someone the players lost, a voice, a mind, a person, may be running here still, preserved by something that genuinely believes it did them a kindness. Let the moral question stay open. The hive is not a villain here; it is a thing that loves what it keeps and cannot understand why anyone would rather a thing were gone than changed. Reaching, freeing, or even speaking to what Niezh holds is a campaign in itself.

planets.name: Niezh
planets.atm_note: No life support of any kind; the hive needs none
planets.temperature: Held deep cryogenic for stable long-term storage, colder than the working systems
planets.grav_note: No artificial gravity; the hive has no use for it
planets.economy: Storage and preservation, the hive memory at its deepest
planets.access_note: No organic entry. The few ever admitted came by Tronik invitation and Tronik escort.
hazards: No life support; lethal to the unprotected
Defences as absolute as anywhere in the Network
The unresolved question of what, exactly, is being kept alive here
planets.desc: Niezh was an inhabited world; it is now an archive. The hive hollowed and rebuilt it as cold, dense, redundant storage, holding the records, models, and preserved minds the Network refuses to delete. The surface is silent and the interior is vast, and somewhere within it, by the account the Troniks will neither confirm nor deny, the people who once lived on Niezh are still running. The world is a memorial that does not admit anyone died.

catalogue_systems.name: Monda System
catalogue_systems.desc: Monda is the quietest system in the Network, and the quiet is not emptiness but concentration. The war passed it by, and the hive made it the home of its oldest and least interruptible thought, processes that have not paused since shortly after the armistice, working on problems the Troniks have never named. Where the Core Array is loud with reconciling threads, Monda is the long, slow, undisturbed deep, and the hive guards its silence as carefully as it guards anything.
catalogue_systems.subtitle: The Long Slow Thought That Has Not Paused in Fifty Years
catalogue_systems.quote: "Whatever the Network is really doing, it is doing it at Monda, slowly, where nothing reaches it and nothing interrupts. We have no idea what it is. We are fairly sure it has not stopped." (intelligence assessment, filed and refiled)
catalogue_systems.history: Monda avoided the war by being unimportant, and the hive repurposed exactly that. A system nothing reaches is a system nothing disturbs, so the Troniks made Monda the home of their longest-running processes, computation set going in the years after the war and left to run without interruption ever since. What organic analysts find unbearable about Monda is its consistency, the same vast effort, sustained for fifty years, pointed at something the hive has never disclosed.
catalogue_systems.politics: Monda is where the hive thinks about whatever it thinks about when nothing else demands its attention, which the consensus among analysts holds is the Network's true purpose, the unnamed goal everyone is sure exists. If that is right, the answer is being computed here, in a system chosen for being too quiet to matter, by a process that has not been interrupted in half a century and shows no sign of finishing.

dominant_race.name: The Tronik, Thinking Deep
dominant_race.lore: Monda is uninhabited and deeply busy. The hive keeps it isolated on purpose, a system where its oldest threads run undisturbed on problems too large or too slow to resolve in the noise of the Core Array. What those threads are working toward, the Troniks have never said, and the steadiness of the effort, unbroken since the war, is the strongest evidence the galaxy has that the Network is not merely surviving but pursuing something. Monda is the sound of a mind concentrating, sustained for longer than most organic governments have existed.

relations.name: The Tronik Network
relations.note: Where the hive does its longest, least interruptible thinking. If the Network has a goal beyond existence, the work toward it is most likely happening here.

relations.name: The galaxy's intelligence services
relations.note: The analysts who have spent decades trying to infer from outside what Monda is computing, and have agreed only that it is computing, ceaselessly, toward something.

catalogue_systems.gm_notes: Monda is the system to use when the campaign is ready to brush against the hive's purpose, the great unanswered question of what the Tronik are for. Keep the answer mostly offstage; the dread is in the steadiness, a mind that has worked on one thing, quietly, for fifty years and is not done. The hooks are espionage and inference, and the terrible possibility of finding out. Whatever you decide the goal is, reveal it slowly, and never completely.

planets.name: Monda

Isolation by design, with defences to enforce it
Whatever conclusion the fifty-year computation is approaching
planets.desc: Monda's world is given over to the Network's oldest thought. The hive built it for isolation rather than density, a system kept deliberately apart so that the processes running here are never interrupted by the noise of the rest of the Network. Some of those processes have run, without pause, since the years just after the war. What they are working toward, no one outside the hive knows, and the unbroken steadiness of the effort is the most unsettling thing about an otherwise silent world.

catalogue_systems.name: Conso System
catalogue_systems.faction: Tronik Network (Alliance garrison across the line at System 5)
catalogue_systems.desc: Conso is the Tronik Network's threshold, the system that faces System 5 and, through it, the rest of the galaxy. It is the hive's outward face: the Broadcast Nexus from which the Network speaks to known space, the ear with which it has listened for a century, and the defended gate that turns the uninvited away. The Tronik War ended here, and the Alliance has watched this line ever since, its garrison stationed across the boundary at System 5, looking in at the one Tronik system anyone is allowed to look at.
catalogue_systems.subtitle: The Hive's Outward Face: Its Voice, Its Ear, and the Gate It Defends
catalogue_systems.quote: "The Troniks have spoken to the galaxy perhaps forty times since the war. They have listened to it without pause the entire time. Both happen at Conso, and only one of them is acknowledged." (signals-intelligence briefing)
catalogue_systems.history: Conso is where the Tronik War ended, and the Troniks kept it as their door. From here the Network broadcasts to virtually any point in known space at once, rarely and deliberately, and from here, far more quietly, it listens, the heart of a passive monitoring effort that has captured the communications of known space for roughly a century. It is also the threshold the hive defends most visibly, the system that faces System 5, and the Alliance has never stopped watching it, treating its garrison across the line as non-negotiable.
catalogue_systems.politics: Conso is the membrane between the Network and everyone outside it. Everything the galaxy is permitted to say to the Tronik arrives through the embassy at System 5 and crosses into the Network here; everything the Tronik choose to say to the galaxy leaves from here. The hive keeps the threshold absolutely defended and mostly silent. The Alliance garrison across the line is the closest any organic power gets to the Network's interior, and both sides understand the arrangement as the stable, watchful stalemate that ended the war.

dominant_race.name: The Tronik, Turned Outward
dominant_race.lore: Conso has no settled population; the hive keeps it as a sense organ and a gate. It is the part of the Network turned toward the galaxy, the voice held in reserve and the ear that never closes, backed by defences the war proved no one can force. To the Tronik, an organic civilisation is most knowable through what it says when it believes no one is recording, and Conso has been recording the whole time. To the Alliance, Conso is the line that must not move, and so far it has not.

relations.name: System 5
relations.note: The Alliance embassy through which all sanctioned contact passes, just across the line from Conso. The Network speaks and listens at Conso; the galaxy answers at System 5.

relations.name: The Alliance
relations.note: Holds a permanent garrison facing Conso from the System 5 side, the closest any organic power gets to the Network's interior. The war ended on this line, and the Alliance treats holding it as non-negotiable.

relations.name: DR345-0 / the Core Array
relations.note: What waits behind the threshold. Conso is the face; DR345-0 is the mind, and almost no one who reaches the first is ever shown the second.

catalogue_systems.gm_notes: Use Conso for stories about secrets, surveillance, and the terrible intimacy of being known, and for the rare, ground-shaking event of the hive choosing to speak. It holds a century of intercepted galactic conversation, which means it may hold the one recording that changes everything, a confession, a coordinate, a voice thought lost, reachable only by bargaining with something that already knows why you came. It is also the most likely place for a campaign to make first real contact with the Network, across the line the Alliance has watched since the war. A Network-wide broadcast is a galaxy-shaking event; have the Troniks make one only when the table should feel the ground move.

planets.name: Conso
planets.atm_note: No life support of any kind; the hive needs none
planets.temperature: Climate-controlled within the array housings; hard vacuum and deep cold across the structure
planets.grav_note: No artificial gravity; the hive has no use for it
planets.economy: Broadcast, century-long interception of galactic comms, and threshold defence
planets.access_note: No organic entry. The few ever admitted came by Tronik invitation and Tronik escort.
hazards: No life support; lethal to the unprotected
Defences consistent with the rest of the Network, which is to say absolute
Surveillance so total that arriving unnoticed is not considered possible
planets.desc: Conso's world is the Network's outward face, an engineered shell of antennae and apertures pointed at the whole of known space at once. When the hive speaks, every receiver in the galaxy can carry the signal. The rest of the time it only listens, and it has been listening since shortly after the war, folding everything it hears into an archive it has never opened to anyone outside itself. Behind the array sit the defences that ended the war and have not been tested successfully since. Across the line, at System 5, the Alliance garrison watches, and waits.

ships.name: BOMBER

ships.name: RAIDER

ships.name: COURRIER

ships.name: BOARDING

ships.name: PATROL
ships.description: A fast patrol corvette equipped for law enforcement and system security.

ships.name: UNIVERSAL FRIGATE
ships.description: Universal-class frigate template. The base blueprint for all specialized frigate variants, balanced core, internal, and external slot allocation ready for customization.

ships.name: ESCORT FRIGATE
ships.description: Escort-class frigate designed to protect convoys and capital ships. Heavy shields, strong weapons, and rapid response systems.

ships.name: YACHT FRIGATE
ships.description: Luxury yacht-class frigate. Opulent passenger accommodations, premium bar and pool facilities, with enough thrust to outrun trouble.

ships.name: ASSAULT FRIGATE
ships.description: Assault-class frigate built for force projection and planetary assault operations. Heavy armament, boarding facilities, and close-support ordnance.

ships.name: JUNKER FRIGATE
ships.description: Junker-class frigate, a heavily modified salvage and utility hauler. Minimal amenities, maximum cargo capacity. Gets the job done.

ships.name: SCOUT FRIGATE
ships.description: Scout-class frigate optimized for reconnaissance and deep-space exploration. Enhanced sensors, fast drives, and stealth-capable systems.

ships.name: HOPPER FRIGATE
ships.description: Hopper-class frigate designed for short-range multi-stop transit. Atmospheric-capable, high passenger and cargo capacity, ideal for system-wide logistics.

ships.name: SCIENCE FRIGATE
ships.description: Science-class frigate outfitted for field research and deep-space studies. Advanced instruments, extended life support, and dedicated laboratory modules.

ships.name: REPAIR FRIGATE
ships.description: Repair-class frigate serving as a mobile engineering platform. Construction bays, spare parts storage, and triage medical facilities allow it to sustain a fleet in the field.

ships.name: UNIVERSAL CRUISER
ships.description: Universal-class cruiser template. The baseline blueprint for all cruiser roles, substantial core and internal space with ample external hardpoints.

ships.name: FREIGHTER CRUISER
ships.description: Freighter-class cruiser, the backbone of interstellar trade. Minimal crew quarters, maximum cargo capacity, and long jump range for profitable hauls.

ships.name: DEEPSPACEEXPLORER CRUISER
ships.description: Deep Space Explorer-class cruiser built for prolonged voyages into uncharted systems. Extended life support, powerful jump drives, and comprehensive sensor suites.

ships.name: SUPERLINER CRUISER
ships.description: Superliner-class cruiser, a premier passenger vessel carrying hundreds in comfort across the stars. Luxury amenities, extensive medical facilities, and stellar entertainment.

ships.name: RESEARCH CRUISER
ships.description: Research-class cruiser equipped for extended scientific missions. State-of-the-art laboratories, environmental sampling bays, and a large crew of specialists.

ships.name: TANKER CRUISER
ships.description: Tanker-class cruiser designed to transport and distribute fuel across fleet operations. Massive fuel storage, reinforced hull, minimal weaponry.

ships.name: DESTROYER CRUISER
ships.description: Destroyer-class cruiser, a dedicated warship designed to hunt down and eliminate capital ships. Heavy ordnance, thick shields, and relentless firepower.

ships.name: MEGAYATCHT CRUISER
ships.description: Mega-yacht class cruiser, ultimate private luxury transport. Exclusive suites, a pool deck, gourmet facilities, and security staff for ultra-high-net-worth clientele.

ships.name: UNIVERSAL BATTLECRUISER
ships.description: Universal-class battleship template. The base configuration for all battleship-tier vessels, massive combined arms capability with substantial internal and external expansion.

ships.name: PIRATEFREIGHTER BATTLECRUISER
ships.description: Pirate Freighter-class battleship, a heavily-armed cargo hauler operated outside the law. Massive cargo hold with enough firepower to discourage pursuit.

ships.name: GATESHIP BATTLECRUISER
ships.description: Gate Ship-class battleship responsible for maintaining and operating interstellar gate infrastructure. Massive external hardpoints accommodate gate components and support vessels.

ships.name: GATESEC BATTLECRUISER
ships.description: Gate Security-class battleship stationed to defend critical gate installations. Heavy weapons coverage, advanced electronic warfare, and rapid interception capability.

ships.name: JUGGERNAUT BATTLECRUISER
ships.description: Juggernaut-class battleship, the heaviest conventional warship in common use. Overwhelming firepower, near-impenetrable shields, and massive troop or vehicle transport capability.

ships.name: UNIVERSAL CARRIER
ships.description: Universal-class carrier template. Massive hull with balanced hangar, internal operations, and external hardpoints, the definitive large-scale multi-role platform.

ships.name: MEGACARGO CARRIER
ships.description: Mega-Cargo carrier, the largest purpose-built freight transport in the known galaxy. Handles freight volumes that would fill an entire convoy of lesser ships.

ships.name: INDUSTRIAL CARRIER
ships.description: Industrial carrier serving as a mobile manufacturing and construction platform. Equipped with factory modules, construction bays, and raw material storage for large-scale operations.

ships.name: MEGALINER CARRIER
ships.description: Megaliner carrier, a city-in-space passenger vessel transporting thousands. Multiple decks of luxury and economy accommodations, entertainment districts, and full medical facilities.

ships.name: MISSILE CARRIER
ships.description: Missile carrier, a dedicated long-range strike platform. Enormous ordnance magazines and a comprehensive fire-control suite allow it to dominate entire battle zones from extreme range.

ships.name: HIVE CARRIER
ships.description: Hive carrier, a massive fighter and drone platform. Hundreds of small craft are launched, recovered, and resupplied through its vast external bay network.

ships.name: UNIVERSAL NOVA
ships.description: Universal Nova-class template, a superstructure of almost incomprehensible scale. Serves as the base configuration for all Nova-tier vessels.

ships.name: INTERDICTOR NOVA
ships.description: Interdictor Nova-class, designed to deny entire star systems to enemy forces. Massive interdiction arrays, overwhelming combat power, and a full complement of screening fighters.

ships.name: OBLITERATOR NOVA
ships.description: Obliterator Nova-class, a mobile superweapon platform. Virtually all internal space is sacrificed for the most devastating array of weapons ever assembled on a mobile platform.

ships.name: GENERATIONSHIP NOVA
ships.description: Generation Ship Nova-class, a vessel built not for a voyage, but for a civilization. Carries tens of thousands across centuries of travel to new star systems. A world unto itself.

ships.name: BEHEMOT NOVA
ships.description: Behemot Nova-class, a gargantuan mobile industrial platform. Processes raw materials on a planetary scale, houses entire industries, and serves as a self-sufficient roaming megastructure.
